### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-WEEKLY-REPORT-SURFACE-INVARIANT-GAP - weekly_report renderer accepts blank report surfaces as valid

- Status: **resolved** (committed in `0e55bb23`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-23).
- Severity: **P1** (official weekly report / lifecycle evidence-clock surface integrity before the report renderer is committed or consumed by later batch3 output, paper, comparison, or pipeline slices).
- Source: Codex strict review of US-short batch3 weekly_report.md renderer first cut (`engine/us_short_weekly_report_renderer.py`, `tests/test_us_short_weekly_report_renderer.py`, `docs/README.md` route row).
- Scope reviewed: current working tree after commits `d89e245e` / `6531ecb9`, with modified `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and untracked `engine/us_short_weekly_report_renderer.py`, `tests/test_us_short_weekly_report_renderer.py`; design authority `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §11.2 / §13 / §18.1 #20-#21 / §18.2; frozen contract `presets/us_short_weekly_report_contract_20260620.json`; `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`; `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding: the renderer correctly loads the frozen 13-section / banner / price-clock contract, but its fail-closed checks are weaker than the stated §11.2 surface invariant. `engine/us_short_weekly_report_renderer.py` line 74 rejects `price_clock` values only when they are `None` or exactly `""`, so whitespace-only values render as if the price clock is present. Lines 106-110 reject a section only when its value is `None`; `""`, `"   "`, `[]`, and `[""]` all render, producing a section title with no real body even though the slice claims every one of the 13 sections must carry content. The same count gate at lines 91-95 only checks integer type and equality, so `section_1=-1` / `section_12=-1` renders even though reminder counts are counts, not signed arbitrary integers. The tests cover missing sections and exact empty-string `price_clock`, but not whitespace-only clock values, empty section strings, empty lists, list entries that are blank, or negative counts.
- Direct evidence (Codex 2026-06-23): an adversarial probe against `render_weekly_report()` returned `ACCEPTED` for `empty-string-section`, `whitespace-section`, `empty-list-section`, `list-empty-string-section`, `whitespace-price-clock`, and `negative-counts`. The normal renderer target still passed 13 tests, proving the shipped tests do not catch this class.
- Why material: `weekly_report.md` is the human-facing official output for §11.2. A renderer that can emit all 13 headings while silently leaving a body empty makes the report look structurally complete when a producer failed to supply real content. A whitespace-only price clock is worse: the banner still appears, but the reader cannot tell which price/news window was used. Negative lifecycle reminder counts can also make the §11.2 count reconcile look "matched" while carrying impossible evidence-clock data. This undermines the whole point of a fail-closed report renderer before later enrichment slices consume it.
- Required repair: make the renderer validate **non-blank semantic content**, not only key presence. Narrow acceptable repair: add a helper that treats strings whose `.strip()` is empty as blank; treats a list/tuple as valid only when it is non-empty and every rendered item is non-blank; rejects `None` entries; and applies that helper to each section body before emitting. Apply the same non-blank string rule to all four `price_clock` fields (and preferably require string-ish canonical values if the existing contract expects strings). Enforce lifecycle reminder counts as non-negative integers, still rejecting bools, and keep the equality check. Do not loosen optional banner behavior; optional elements may still be omitted, but if supplied they should not render as blank whitespace.
- Tests required: add adversarial tests proving `""`, whitespace-only strings, empty lists, lists of blank strings, and `None` list entries are refused for any required section; whitespace-only `price_clock` fields are refused; matched negative counts are refused; zero counts remain valid. Keep the existing positive controls for 13-section frozen order, optional banner element present/absent, exact missing price_clock, count mismatch, and malformed top-level input.
- Verification evidence (Codex 2026-06-23): `python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_weekly_report_renderer` = 13 OK; `py_compile` for renderer/test OK; `tests.test_doc_governance_guard tests.test_route_doc_ledger_status_consistency` = 39 OK before closeout; `git diff --check` reports only the existing CRLF warning for `docs/README.md`; BOM/FFFD false for the renderer/test/contract. Full `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*us_short*'` cannot complete in this Codex bundled runtime because `jsonschema` is absent, causing 35 unrelated existing schema/validator imports to fail before test bodies (533 tests attempted, 35 errors, 1 skip).
- Boundary: repair only the weekly_report renderer surface-invariant gap and direct tests / route-doc wording if needed. Do not start provider/live/network/full-market fetch, DataHub, Skill, production work, broker/order integration, A-share review/implementation, US-long work, paper/live-normalized fill, comparison shadow, lifecycle eval changes outside direct count input validation, or later exclusion_summary / hot_excluded / coverage-honesty enrichment under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-23, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged valid + in-scope + necessary, accepted — same partial-validation class: I checked key presence / `None` / exact `""`, not the whole BLANK / EMPTY / NEGATIVE class, so a structurally-complete-but-empty §11.2 surface still rendered. Fixed all three fail-closed invariants per the Required: (1) added `_section_has_content` — a section body must be a non-blank string OR a non-empty list/tuple whose EVERY item is a non-blank string (`''` / whitespace / `[]` / `['']` / `[None]` / `['ok','']` / non-str all refused); (2) the 4 price_clock fields now require a non-blank string (`_nonblank_str` — whitespace-only refused, not only None/''); (3) the lifecycle counts must be NON-NEGATIVE ints (still reject bool, keep the equality check; zero stays valid, so a negative count can't fake a "matched" reconcile). Optional banner ①②③⑤ render only when supplied non-blank (a blank optional is omitted, never rendered as `②: `). Whole-class: every DISPLAYED surface value (section body / price_clock / count / optional banner) now has a non-blank / non-negative gate. Tests added (`SurfaceInvariantFailsClosed`): the 6 Codex probes + `[None]` + mixed-blank list refused, whitespace price_clock refused, negative counts refused, zero counts valid (positive control), blank optional omitted; existing positive controls kept. B-ripple: README renderer route row updated (non-blank content / non-negative counts / blank-optional-omitted). Verify: renderer **18 OK** (+5); full offline `*us_short*` 1177 OK zero regression; doc/route guard 25 OK; direct probe — all 6 named cases + 2 more refused while zero-counts renders; BOM/FFFD false; `git diff --check` CRLF-only. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.
- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-23): **PASS**. Confirmed the current renderer closes `R-USSHORT-BATCH3-WEEKLY-REPORT-SURFACE-INVARIANT-GAP`: `_nonblank_str` requires non-blank strings for all price-clock fields, `_section_has_content` rejects empty / whitespace / empty-list / blank-item / `None` / non-string section bodies, lifecycle counts must be non-bool nonnegative ints and still match, and blank optional banner values are omitted rather than rendered. Direct probes refuse the six previously accepted cases (`empty-string-section`, `whitespace-section`, `empty-list-section`, `list-empty-string-section`, `whitespace-price-clock`, `negative-counts`) plus `[None]` and mixed-blank lists; zero counts still render. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-READINESS-ASOF-REAL-DATE-GAP - tracked lifecycle readiness writer accepts impossible as_of dates

- Status: **resolved** (committed in `0ad2d7af`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-23).
- Severity: **P1** (PIT / lifecycle readiness integrity before the weekly_report lifecycle section, top banner, and count reconcile consume the tracked readiness artifact).
- Source: Codex strict review of US-short batch3 R2 lifecycle-eval slice 2c second cut (`schemas/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.schema.json` + `engine/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.py`).
- Scope reviewed: current working tree after commits `198aff9b` / `e3c4d6eb`, with modified `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval.py`, `engine/us_short_lifecycle_render.py`, `engine/us_short_lifecycle_store.py`, and untracked `engine/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.py`, `schemas/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.schema.json`, `tests/test_us_short_lifecycle_readiness.py`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_lifecycle_readiness_schema.py`; design authority `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §2 / §3.5 / §11.2 / §11.6 / §13 / §18.1 #20 / §18.2; `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`; `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding: the new readiness artifact correctly narrows tracked content to `schema_name`, `schema_version`, `as_of`, `total_items`, `due_count`, `due_items`, and `upgrade_eligible_items`, and rejects extra ticker/performance fields through `additionalProperties:false`. However `schemas/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.schema.json` defines `as_of` only as `"pattern": "^[0-9]{8}$"` (line 12), and `engine/us_short_lifecycle_readiness.py::_assert_readiness` adds only `due_count == len(due_items)`, item-number range, and `upgrade ⊆ due` checks (lines 47-60). It does not re-apply the strict real-date gate already used by `validate_lifecycle_register` and `lifecycle_banner`. A local schema-equivalent probe shows `_assert_readiness` accepts `{"as_of": "20260231", ...}` and `write_lifecycle_readiness` writes that impossible date to JSON before any weekly renderer would consume it; the same probe confirmed the existing `due_count` cross-field gate still rejects mismatches.
- Why material: this artifact is explicitly the tracked due-scan summary that the weekly_report lifecycle section, top banner, and §11.2 count reconcile will consume. The design treats `as_of` / decision-date anchoring as PIT state, and adjacent lifecycle surfaces already reject impossible dates (`validate_lifecycle_register` rejects `20260231`; the runtime banner returns `UNAVAILABLE`). Letting the public tracked readiness artifact accept a non-real date can mis-anchor a lifecycle reminder / reconcile output while still looking schema-clean, which undermines the evidence-clock and weekly-report integrity gate.
- Required repair: add a strict real-date validation for readiness `as_of` before any readiness artifact is emitted or written. The narrow repair can reuse the lifecycle eval date helper or implement the same contract locally: string, ASCII, exactly 8 digits, and valid calendar `YYYYMMDD`. The check must run in `_assert_readiness`, so both `build_lifecycle_readiness` and `write_lifecycle_readiness` are protected. Update the schema description / README route row if needed so the active contract no longer implies pattern-only date validation is sufficient.
- Tests required: add module tests proving `write_lifecycle_readiness` / `_assert_readiness` reject impossible, malformed, non-ASCII, and non-string `as_of` values without leaving a file; keep a positive control for a valid real date. Add or extend schema tests / contract tests to document the schema-vs-engine split if draft-07 keeps the regex-only pattern. Rerun the readiness target, schema target, full offline `*us_short*` if available, and doc/route guards.
- Verification evidence (Codex 2026-06-23): bundled Python has no `jsonschema` (`importlib.util.find_spec("jsonschema") is None`), so `tests.test_us_short_lifecycle_readiness` and `tests.schema.test_us_short_lifecycle_readiness_schema` fail at import with `ModuleNotFoundError`; `requirements.txt` still records `jsonschema>=4.0`. `py_compile` for the new module/tests OK; doc/route guards 39 OK; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM/FFFD false for touched/new files. Static review plus a schema-equivalent local probe reproduced the gap: `ASSERT_ACCEPTED_IMPOSSIBLE_AS_OF`, `WRITE_ACCEPTED_IMPOSSIBLE_AS_OF 20260231`, while `DUECOUNT_REJECTED LifecycleReadinessError`.
- Boundary: repair only lifecycle readiness `as_of` strict-real-date validation and directly associated tests/docs wording. Do not start weekly_report lifecycle section/top banner, §11.2 count reconcile, weekly renderer, provider/live/DataHub/Skill/production, broker/order, A-share, or US-long work under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-23, working tree; 用户 `执行` 命令下 — judged serial-gate priority: a pending FAIL must clear before the next E+F build slice, so this readiness FAIL was repaired first rather than stacking new work): judged valid + in-scope + necessary, accepted — the readiness `as_of` gate did the schema's 8-digit pattern but NOT a strict REAL date, so `20260231` (Feb 31) passed `_assert_readiness` + `write_lifecycle_readiness` (the same partial-date-validation class already closed in `validate_lifecycle_register` / `lifecycle_banner`). Fixed: imported the canonical `_strict_yyyymmdd` from `engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval` (single source — the Required sanctions reuse) and added a strict-real-date check in `_assert_readiness` immediately after the schema gate, so BOTH `build_lifecycle_readiness` (self-check) and `write_lifecycle_readiness` (write gate) reject an impossible / malformed / non-ASCII / non-string `as_of` before any artifact is emitted or written. Whole-class: `as_of` is the ONLY date field in the readiness contract → one leg, now closed. B-ripple: the schema description + README route row no longer imply the 8-digit pattern is sufficient (both now state the `as_of` strict-real-date is engine-enforced). Tests: `ReadinessAsOfRealDate` (assert + write reject `20260231` leaving no file; wrong-len / non-digit / non-string / non-ASCII rejected; valid real date passes). Verify: readiness 16 OK (+4); full offline `*us_short*` 1139 OK + schema `*us_short*` 472 OK zero regression; doc/route guard 25 OK; direct probe — assert/write reject `20260231` (no file), valid date passes; BOM/FFFD false; `git diff --check` CRLF-only. ### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-BANNER-FAILCLOSED-GBK-GAP - lifecycle runtime banner trusts malformed eval output and can break GBK safety

- Status: **resolved** (committed in `198aff9b`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-23).
- Severity: **P1** (runtime lifecycle reminder / evidence-clock visibility before weekly lifecycle section, readiness artifact, and weekly renderer consume the eval stage).
- Source: Codex strict review of US-short batch3 R2 lifecycle-eval slice 2c first cut (`engine/us_short_lifecycle_render.py` GBK-safe runtime banner).
- Scope reviewed: current working tree after commits `bc74b36f` / `5a8de744`, with modified `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and untracked `engine/us_short_lifecycle_render.py`, `tests/test_us_short_lifecycle_render.py`; design authority `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §13 / §12.2 / §18.1 #20 / §18.2; route row `docs/README.md` US-short batch3 R2 slice 2c. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding: `lifecycle_banner` only checks that `total_items` is an `int` and that `due_items` / `upgrade_eligible_items` are lists, then formats `as_of`, list members, and counts directly. It does not require `due_count`, does not check `due_count == len(due_items)`, does not reject negative / impossible totals, and does not require `as_of`, due item ids, or upgrade item ids to be ASCII-safe canonical values before rendering. Direct probes show: missing `due_count` renders a normal `0/39` banner; `due_count=2` with `due_items=[]` renders `0/39` and hides the due reminder; `due_count=0` with `due_items=[1,2]` renders `2/39 DUE`; `total_items=-1` renders `0/-1`; emoji `as_of`, due item id, or upgrade id produce a non-ASCII banner whose `.encode("gbk")` raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, not `UNAVAILABLE`.
- Why material: this slice's purpose is specifically to make §13 lifecycle reminders visible as a GBK-safe runtime banner and to fail closed on malformed / missing eval results so a reminder is never hidden by an empty or misleading string. A malformed due-scan result can currently be presented as a clean no-due state, and malformed strings can break the GBK console path the slice exists to protect. That undermines the runtime reminder gate before the weekly report / readiness artifact work lands.
- Required repair: validate the eval-result contract before rendering, or normalize through a closed helper. Required invariants: dict input; `total_items` is a non-bool positive integer; `due_count` is a non-bool nonnegative integer and equals `len(due_items)`; `len(due_items) <= total_items`; `due_items` and `upgrade_eligible_items` contain only expected lifecycle item numbers (non-bool positive ints; preferably within the enrolled item range / total); upgrade ids are a subset of due ids; `as_of` is either absent/unknown or a strict ASCII-safe lifecycle date. Any violation must return the conservative `UNAVAILABLE - treat as NOT clean` banner. After formatting, the returned banner should be guaranteed ASCII (or at minimum guaranteed `.encode("gbk")`), with tests proving malformed non-ASCII values cannot leak into output.
- Tests required: add adversarial tests for missing `due_count`, both `due_count` mismatch directions, negative / zero / too-small `total_items`, non-int/bool/emoji due ids, non-int/bool/emoji upgrade ids, upgrade ids not due, non-ASCII / invalid `as_of`, and a final ASCII/GBK assertion over both valid and malformed paths. Keep positive controls for no-due, due-items listed, upgrade-eligible surfaced but never acted on, and integration from `evaluate_lifecycle`.
- Verification evidence (Codex 2026-06-23): `py_compile` for render/test OK; doc/route guards 39 OK; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM/FFFD false; direct adversarial probes above reproduce the malformed normal-banner and non-GBK output paths. Target `tests.test_us_short_lifecycle_render` and full offline `*us_short*` could not be executed to completion in this runtime because the current bundled Python lacks `jsonschema` (`importlib.util.find_spec("jsonschema") is None`), causing imports through `engine.us_short_lifecycle_eval` / schema tests to fail before test bodies. This verification gap does not excuse the direct banner bug.
- Boundary: repair only lifecycle banner input-contract / fail-closed / ASCII-GBK guard wiring and directly associated tests/docs wording. Do not start readiness artifact, weekly-report lifecycle section/top banner, count reconcile, weekly renderer, provider/live/DataHub/Skill/production, broker/order, A-share, or US-long work under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-23, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged valid + in-scope + necessary, accepted — my banner TRUSTED the eval-result content (clean as_of date, clean int ids) instead of validating it (the same partial-input-validation class). Fixed: added `_validated(eval_result)` enforcing the FULL contract before rendering — dict input; total_items a non-bool positive int; due_items / upgrade_eligible_items are lists of UNIQUE non-bool positive ints within [1, total]; due_count a non-bool nonneg int == len(due_items); len(due_items) <= total; upgrade ⊆ due; as_of absent/unknown OR a strict ASCII YYYYMMDD — ANY violation returns the conservative UNAVAILABLE banner (never a misleading 0-due banner). The returned banner is GUARANTEED ASCII (a final `.encode('ascii')` floor → UNAVAILABLE if it ever failed), so a malformed non-ASCII as_of / id can never leak to the GBK console. Kept the module jsonschema-free + made the integration test import `evaluate_lifecycle` LAZILY (skip if absent), so the banner suite runs on a minimal runtime (closes the Codex verification gap). Tests added (`BannerContractFailsClosed` + extended `BannerAsciiGbkSafe`): missing / both-direction-mismatch due_count, negative / zero / too-small / non-int / bool total, non-int / bool / emoji / duplicate / out-of-range due ids, non-int / emoji / not-due upgrade ids, non-ASCII / wrong-len / impossible / int as_of, ASCII+GBK over valid AND emoji paths with a no-leak assertion; positive controls kept (no-due, due listed, upgrade surfaced-not-acted, as_of-absent→unknown, evaluate_lifecycle integration). Verify: render 13 OK (+5); full offline `*us_short*` 1116 OK + schema `*us_short*` 465 OK zero regression; doc/route guard 25 OK; direct probes — due_count mismatch / negative total → UNAVAILABLE, emoji as_of / id → UNAVAILABLE + GBK-safe + no leak, positive control intact; BOM/FFFD false; `git diff --check` CRLF-only. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-23): **PASS** scoped to the lifecycle banner repair. Confirmed the prior fail-closed / GBK gap is closed in the current working tree: `lifecycle_banner` validates the eval-result contract before rendering; bad or missing `due_count`, both mismatch directions, negative totals, emoji / non-int / invalid ids, upgrade-not-due, and non-ASCII / invalid `as_of` all return the ASCII/GBK-safe `UNAVAILABLE` banner; valid no-due and due / upgrade banners still render with the user-decision caveat. Verification: `tests.test_us_short_lifecycle_render` 13 OK with 1 expected skip for the optional `evaluate_lifecycle` integration when `jsonschema` is absent; `py_compile` OK; doc/route guards 39 OK; direct probes over valid + malformed paths all encode as ASCII and GBK with no non-ASCII leak; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM/FFFD false. Full offline `*us_short*` and schema suites remain unverified in this Codex runtime because the bundled Python lacks `jsonschema` (`find_spec=None`), causing unrelated schema/eval imports to fail. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-MALFORMED-INPUT-EDGES - lifecycle accumulator / authority validator still accept or raw-raise malformed edge inputs

- Status: **resolved** (committed in `5efb4f0a`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-23).
- Severity: **P1** (lifecycle evidence-clock / clean-gate correctness before the runtime persister, weekly lifecycle banner, readiness artifact, or upgrade-review routing consumes this accumulator).
- Source: Codex strict review of US-short batch3 R2 lifecycle-eval slice 2a (derived `forward_observations` ledger + idempotent `accumulate_lifecycle_observation`).
- Scope reviewed: current working tree with modified `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval.py`, `schemas/us_short_lifecycle_register.schema.json`, and `tests/test_us_short_lifecycle_eval.py`; recent commits through `1a219321`; `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §2.1 / §12.2 / §13 / §13.1 / §13.2 / §18.0 / §18.1 #20 / §18.2; `docs/AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`; `docs/pre_codex_self_review_checklist.md`; prior batch3 cut1/R2a/lifecycle slice-1 route rows and tests. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding 1: `engine/us_short_lifecycle_eval.py::accumulate_lifecycle_observation` documents that malformed observation input raises `LifecycleObservationError`, but each per-item update dict silently ignores unknown keys. Direct probes on a clean register: `{1: {"forward_contribution_typo": 1}}` returned a clean register with derived count `0`; `{1: {"forward_contribution": 1, "unexpected": 123}}` returned a clean register with count `1`; `{1: {"secondary_condition_met": false, "extra_flag": true}}` returned clean. This means a typo or stale producer field can be silently dropped or partially applied while the function reports success.
- Technical finding 2: `validate_lifecycle_register` validates an injected/loaded threshold authority against the const-pinned authority schema, records schema violations, but then continues authority cross-ref checks with untrusted values in membership tests. Direct probes with malformed authority values produced raw `TypeError` instead of `{"clean": false, ...}`: `item_category["1"] = ["bad"]`, `item_category["1"] = {"bad": 1}`, and `category_thresholds["scoring weight"]["count_type"] = ["weeks"]`. This reopens the malformed-input fail-closed class at the authority edge; a future corrupt authority file or bad test injection can crash the clean gate before controlled lifecycle refusal.
- Why material: slice 2a is the first lifecycle producer API. Batch3's contract is not just "do not overcount"; it is "producer never emits or launders a not-clean accumulator, and validator malformed input fails closed." Silently accepting unknown update fields can lose lifecycle observations or partially mutate state while claiming success, which corrupts the evidence clock in the undercount direction and hides producer bugs. Raw `TypeError` at the authority edge breaks the controlled fail-closed contract that downstream runtime/persister stages will depend on before rendering reminders or readiness artifacts.

In `accumulate_lifecycle_observation`, reject any per-item update key outside the allowed set `{forward_contribution, secondary_condition_met, upgrade_margin_frozen}` with `LifecycleObservationError`, before applying any partial mutation for that item. In `validate_lifecycle_register`, type-guard authority cross-ref checks after schema validation so malformed authority values cannot be used as unhashable membership keys; either skip dependent semantic checks once the authority schema has failed, or add explicit scalar/string guards that record violations and continue safely. If `accumulate_lifecycle_observation` sees a not-clean or malformed base/authority, it should raise `LifecycleObservationError`, not leak raw `TypeError`.

Keep existing positive controls: same-date idempotence, distinct-date accumulation, weeks 0/1 rule, triggers multi-per-date, governed due, and shipped authority clean.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-MALFORMED-INPUT-RAISES - lifecycle validator raises TypeError for malformed item keys instead of failing closed

- Status: **resolved** (committed in `ceb79483`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-22).
- Severity: **P1** (clean-gate robustness before downstream lifecycle runtime / weekly_report consumers rely on the validator's fail-closed contract).
- Source: Codex full strict review of US-short batch3 R2 lifecycle-eval slice 1.
- Scope reviewed: same current R2 lifecycle slice as `R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2-LIFECYCLE-THRESHOLD-SELF-AUTHORING-BYPASS`; no provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/broker/order/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding: the module docstring and README route row state malformed input fails closed and never raises, and the structural jsonschema gate does record schema errors. But after collecting schema errors, `validate_lifecycle_register` continues semantic checks that use untrusted values as dict/set keys. Direct probes on an otherwise full valid register produced `TypeError` instead of `{"clean": false, ...}` for `items[0].number = ["bad"]`, `items[0].number = {"bad": 1}`, `items[0].threshold_category = ["category"]`, and `items[0].threshold_category = {"category": 1}`. Sibling bad types for `count_type`, `threshold_min_count`, `live_forward_count`, `secondary_condition_met`, and `due` returned `clean=False` without raising, so the raising class is specifically the unhashable membership/set path for number/category.
- Why material: lifecycle eval is a pre-render clean gate. A malformed private lifecycle register should be reported as not-clean so the runtime can fail closed with a controlled error and leave no misleading reminder output. Raising an uncaught `TypeError` from the validator contradicts the public contract and can crash future consumers before they receive structured violations, while tests currently exercise only `None`, scalar, and wrong `items` shape.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-R2A-RENDER-VALIDATE-FALSE-BYPASS - action_table renderer exposes a public opt-out that can render a not-clean machine record

- Status: **resolved** (Codex `review FAIL` 2026-06-22 → Claude `修复` 2026-06-22; committed in `37188a55`, Codex re-`审查 PASS`).
- Severity: **P1** (output-contract / clean-gate integrity before downstream weekly_report, private packet, paper-fill, comparison, or lifecycle consumers trust rendered rows).
- Source: Codex adversarial review of US-short batch3 R2a `action_table.csv` renderer.
- Scope reviewed: `engine/us_short_action_table_renderer.py`, `tests/test_us_short_action_table_renderer.py`, `docs/README.md` R2a route row, top `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, current `docs/system_risk_register.md`, `engine/us_short_private_paths.py`, `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, and the frozen `us_short_action_table_contract` preset/schema route. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share/US-long path was run.
- Technical finding: the slice claims `render_action_table(machine_record)` consumes only a §10-clean machine layer and refuses not-clean records. The module docstring says the renderer "consumes ONLY a validated machine layer" and "never half-rendered"; the README R2a row says it "REFUSES a record the §10 no-dangling validator doesn't mark clean." But the public API is `render_action_table(machine_record, *, validate=True)`, and `tests/test_us_short_action_table_renderer.py::Render.test_validate_false_skips_the_gate` intentionally proves that `validate=False` renders a record with `final_action="invalid_action"` instead of raising. Direct probe on the current working tree confirmed: default render raises `NotCleanMachineRecordError`; `render_action_table(bad, validate=False)` returns one row whose `final_action` cell is `invalid_action`; `write_action_table(bad, outside_path)` still raises and leaves no file.
- Why material: batch3 R2a is the first output renderer built on top of the §10 validator. The design says CSV/weekly report are rendered from the machine layer with the validator welded at the machine layer, and report generation must not proceed when the record is not clean. A public opt-out creates a sanctioned bypass for future callers, tests, or downstream renderers to emit an action_table from a schema/validator-invalid machine record, even though the route docs and module contract say this cannot happen. The private-path persister is safer by default, but the renderer contract itself is false.
- Required repair: remove the public clean-gate opt-out or make it inaccessible to production renderer callers. The narrow preferred repair is to delete the `validate` parameter from `render_action_table`, always run `validate_machine_record`, and replace `test_validate_false_skips_the_gate` with an adversarial test proving there is no bypass: a not-clean record always raises, including when a caller tries to pass an unexpected `validate=False` argument if the signature is removed. If a test-only helper is truly needed, it must be private, clearly named as unsafe/test-only, not used by `render_action_table`, not documented as part of the renderer API, and must not weaken the R2a route claim.
- Tests required: update R2a tests so the official renderer has no clean-gate bypass; keep positive controls for a clean record rendering all 51 frozen columns, omitted columns rendering empty, cell formatting, `write_action_table` private-path guard ordering, and not-clean records leaving no file. Add or adjust a direct public-API test so `render_action_table` cannot be called in a way that emits a table from a bad machine record.
- Verification expected: R2a target tests pass; R2a + cut1 no-dangling/schema tests pass; full offline `*us_short*` stays green; schema `*us_short*` stays green; doc/route guards stay green after closeout entries; direct probe shows the former `validate=False` bypass no longer emits invalid `final_action`; `git diff --check` has only existing line-ending warnings if any.
- Boundary: repair only the R2a renderer clean-gate bypass and any directly associated tests/docs wording. Do not start weekly_report renderer, paper/live-normalized fill, comparison shadow, lifecycle eval, provider health, DataHub, Skill, production, broker/order, A-share, or US-long work under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged valid + in-scope + necessary, accepted — the `validate=False` opt-out was a sanctioned clean-gate bypass that falsified the renderer's "consumes ONLY a validated machine layer / never half-rendered" contract, and I had even written `test_validate_false_skips_the_gate` BLESSING the bypass. Took Codex's preferred narrow fix: DELETED the `validate` parameter from `render_action_table` — it now ALWAYS runs `validate_machine_record` and raises `NotCleanMachineRecordError` on a not-clean record (no opt-out; the §10 gate is welded at the machine layer per §11.1). Replaced the bless-the-bypass test with `test_no_clean_gate_bypass` (a not-clean record always raises, AND `render_action_table(bad, validate=False)` now raises `TypeError` — the parameter is gone). `write_action_table` already called `render_action_table` with no `validate` kwarg, so it is unaffected; the module docstring + README R2a row ("never half-rendered / refuses not-clean") are now TRUE with no caveat. Verify: direct probe — default render raises `NotCleanMachineRecordError`, `validate=False` raises `TypeError` (bypass gone), a clean record still renders; R2a 16 OK, full offline `*us_short*` 1004 OK zero regression; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM=0. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-ACTION-TABLE-VOCAB-BYPASS - machine-record clean gate accepts row vocab values outside the frozen action-table contract

- Status: **resolved** (Codex `review FAIL` 2026-06-22 → Claude `修复` 2026-06-22; committed in the 2026-06-22 batch3 cut1 build `5c399107`, Codex re-`审查 PASS`).
- Severity: **P1** (schema/output-contract integrity before any renderer/private packet/action-table writer consumes the machine record).
- Source: Codex adversarial review of US-short batch3 cut1 no-dangling validator.
- Scope reviewed: `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, `schemas/us_short_machine_record_contract.schema.json`, `tests/test_us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_machine_record_contract_schema.py`, `presets/us_short_action_table_contract_20260620.json`, `presets/us_short_field_registry_governance_20260620.json`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md`, and the top `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` batch3 startup entry. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share path was run.
- Technical finding: the machine-record schema deliberately keeps the large vocabularies out of draft-07 and says runtime membership is enforced by `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py` from the frozen `us_short_action_table_contract`. The validator currently reads `core_columns` only for landing-target checks and does not enforce `design_locked_enums` on row values. `final_action` is only checked when the row has a hard veto, and the schema only requires it to be a non-empty string. Direct probe: mutate the non-hard-veto holding row to `final_action="invalid_action"` and `validate_machine_record(...)` still returns `clean=True` with no violations.
- Why material: batch3 cut1 is the shared clean gate that later renderer / private weekly packet / CSV surfaces are supposed to consume. If an invalid `final_action`, `row_source`, or any present row field covered by `design_locked_enums` can pass as clean, the "single frozen action-table contract" claim is false and downstream report generation can emit a value outside the authoritative action vocabulary.
- Required repair: enforce action-table frozen enum membership in the validator without copying the vocabularies. Load `action_table["design_locked_enums"]`; for every row field that is present and has a frozen enum, require the value to be a member of that enum. At minimum this must cover required row fields `row_source` and `final_action`; it should also cover any additional row fields carried by the flexible machine layer when their names appear in `design_locked_enums` (`coverage_status`, `live_permission_status`, `theme_lifecycle_state`, etc.). Keep terminal landing checks (`terminal_surface_target` in `core_columns`) separate from value membership. Add adversarial tests proving invalid `final_action` and invalid `row_source` fail even without a hard veto, plus at least one optional design-locked enum field if the machine row carries it. Keep the schema as structural-only unless the repair deliberately documents that value membership lives only in the validator.
- Verification expected: targeted batch3 validator/schema tests fail before the fix and pass after; full offline `*us_short*` stays green; schema/action-table governance tests stay green; adversarial probe above returns `clean=False`; no provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share execution is needed.
- Boundary: repair this batch3 cut1 clean-gate class only. Do not start renderer, private writer, paper/live normalized evidence, comparison shadow, lifecycle eval, provider health, DataHub, Skill, production, broker/order, or any A-share work under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged valid + in-scope + necessary, accepted — I had deliberately under-scoped (left action-table enum membership to the action_table schema), but the §10 validator IS the clean gate the renderer / private packet / CSV consume, so a garbage `final_action` passing as `clean=True` falsifies the single-frozen-contract claim. Fix in `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`: load `action_table["design_locked_enums"]` (no hardcoded copy) and for EVERY present row field whose name has a frozen enum, require the value ∈ that enum — WHOLE-CLASS over all 14 enum columns, not only the two named. Required fields (`row_source` / `final_action`) must be non-empty AND a member; optional categoricals (`observe_reason_type` / `coverage_status` / …) may be empty/NA (skipped — a legitimately not-applicable empty is NOT false-failed, reverse-control) but if present-non-empty must be a member. Terminal-landing checks (`terminal_surface_target` ∈ `core_columns`) kept separate from value membership; schema stays structural-only. Tests (tests/test_us_short_no_dangling_validator.py::ActionTableVocab): invalid `final_action` WITHOUT a hard veto → `clean=False` (Codex's exact probe), invalid `row_source`, invalid optional enum, empty required field, + positive controls (valid optional enum / empty optional not false-failed / baseline). Verify: validator 51 OK, full offline `*us_short*` 963 OK, action_table governance tests green, the reproduced `clean=True` bypass now returns `clean=False`; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM=0. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH3-PIT-EVIDENCE-TRACEBACK-GAP - malformed run PIT date and nullable evidence kind can pass the evidence-traceback clean gate

- Status: **resolved** (Codex `review FAIL` 2026-06-22 → Claude `修复` 2026-06-22; committed in the 2026-06-22 batch3 cut1 build `5c399107`, Codex re-`审查 PASS`).
- Severity: **P1** (PIT/evidence-traceback integrity before private machine records become the renderer's authority).
- Source: Codex adversarial review of US-short batch3 cut1 no-dangling validator.
- Scope reviewed: `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, `schemas/us_short_machine_record_contract.schema.json`, `tests/test_us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_machine_record_contract_schema.py`, `presets/us_short_field_registry_governance_20260620.json`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` section 10 / section 11.1 / section 18, and the top `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` batch3 startup entry. No provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share path was run.
- Technical finding:
  1. Run-level `record["as_of"]` is not validated as a strict real `YYYYMMDD` unless a claim has an `evidence_ref.as_of` and that evidence date is already strict. A machine record with `as_of="20260231"` and no claims returns `clean=True`; the schema regex also accepts impossible calendar dates because it only checks 8 digits.
  2. For a claim, `evidence_ref_kind` may be `None` while `evidence_ref.kind` is present and valid. The validator only reports a declaration mismatch when `decl_kind is not None`, so a claim with no registry-declared evidence kind still returns `clean=True` as long as the runtime `evidence_ref.kind` is valid. Direct probe: mutate the valid theme claim to `evidence_ref_kind=None` and `validate_machine_record(...)` returns `clean=True`.
- Why material: design section 10 requires every claim to trace to provider row / SEC filing / source_id at the record's PIT `as_of`, and the batch3 startup entry claims strict 8-digit + real-date `as_of` and declared-kind equality. The current gate lets a private machine record have no valid run PIT anchor, and lets claim evidence bypass the registry declaration that should make traceback auditable.
- Required repair: validate top-level `record["as_of"]` with the existing strict real-date helper before row iteration and mark the record not clean on missing / malformed / impossible dates, independent of whether any row has claims. For every non-null `claim_type`, require a non-null/non-empty `evidence_ref_kind` that belongs to `evidence_ref_kinds` and exactly equals `evidence_ref.kind`; a null declaration is valid only for non-claim field records. Keep existing checks for `evidence_ref.kind`, `value`, and evidence date matching the run PIT. Add adversarial tests for invalid run-level `as_of` with no claims, missing run-level `as_of`, claim with `evidence_ref_kind=None`, and claim declaration mismatch; preserve positive controls for non-claim records with nullable evidence metadata.
- Verification expected: targeted batch3 tests fail before the fix and pass after; adversarial probes above return `clean=False`; full offline `*us_short*` stays green; schema tests document the structural-vs-semantic split if regex-only date shape remains in draft-07; no provider/live/network/DataHub/Skill/production/A-share execution is needed.
- Boundary: repair only batch3 cut1 PIT/evidence-traceback validation and its tests/docs claims. Do not start downstream writer/renderer/comparison/lifecycle/provider/DataHub/Skill/production work under this Required.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged both sub-issues valid + in-scope, accepted — they are real holes my own 起草 entry claimed were closed. Fix in `engine/us_short_no_dangling_validator.py`: ① validate the run-level `record["as_of"]` with the existing strict real-date helper BEFORE row iteration — missing / malformed / impossible (e.g. `20260231`, which the 8-digit schema regex accepts) → not clean, INDEPENDENT of whether any row carries a claim; ② for every non-null `claim_type`, require a non-null `evidence_ref_kind` ∈ `evidence_ref_kinds` (the existing declared==actual-kind match kept) — a null registry declaration is valid ONLY for non-claim field records, so a claim can no longer bypass the registry declaration even when the runtime `evidence_ref.kind` is valid. Schema left structural-only; added a schema test documenting the structural-vs-semantic date split (the regex accepts `20260231`; real-date validity lives in the validator). Tests (RunLevelPitAndClaimDeclaration): impossible run `as_of` with NO claims → `clean=False`, missing run `as_of` → `clean=False`, claim with `evidence_ref_kind=None` → `clean=False` (Codex's probe), claim with a non-frozen declared kind → `clean=False`, + positive controls (valid run `as_of` / non-claim field may keep a null declaration). Verify: validator 51 OK + schema 16 OK, full offline `*us_short*` 963 OK, both reproduced `clean=True` bypasses now return `clean=False`; `git diff --check` CRLF-only; BOM=0. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

### R-USSHORT-CANONICAL-DECISION-ACTIVE-SESSION-ROLL-GAP - canonical US-short decision date rolls after RTH open before the price basis has settled

- Status: **resolved** (Codex `review FAIL` 2026-06-22 → Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, design-only working tree; closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`).
- Severity: **P2** (PIT / price-clock design contract gap; it blocks closing this design change before batch-4 implementation, but does not indicate an existing US-short runner/runtime failure because that runner does not exist yet).
- Scope reviewed: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` section 2 title, section 2.1 canonical decision-date block, section 3.5 calendar/timezone note, section 11.2 price-clock banner, and section 18.2 batch-4 implementation row. No provider call, live run, DataHub, broker/order path, A-share path, engine scoring, schema behavior, or batch-4 code was touched.
- Technical finding: the new canonical block says that Friday close / weekend / Monday pre-open runs resolve to Monday, but a Monday run **after RTH open** rolls the canonical `decision_date` to Tuesday. The same block and the price-clock banner also say that price data is based on the canonical decision day's previous closed trading day. During Monday 09:30-16:00 ET, Tuesday's previous closed trading day is Monday, but Monday is not closed yet. A literal batch-4 implementation would therefore either use stale Friday prices for an early Tuesday decision, or violate the stated "previous closed trading day" clock.
- Why material: US-short batch-4 is intended to create private weekly packets and forward evidence buckets keyed by `decision_date`. A resolver that advances to the next decision date during an active session can contaminate the next decision packet with an unsettled/stale price basis and blur the live/historical evidence boundary. The issue is cheaper to fix now because this is still design-only.
- Required repair: define the live canonical window with both edges: it starts only after the previous trading session has closed (including early-close calendar handling) and ends before the target decision session's RTH open. If the system is run after the target session opens but before that same session closes, the batch-4 design must fail closed / out-of-window and must not emit a new private packet or forward-evidence decision for the next trading day. Only after the current session closes may the resolver roll to the next trading day, with the just-closed session as the price basis. Update the section 2.1 canonical block and the batch-4 test expectations in section 18.2; update section 3.5 / section 11.2 if needed so calendar, half-day, DST, and price-clock wording remain consistent.
- Verification expected: the repaired design has explicit injected-calendar test requirements for Friday close/weekend/Monday pre-open resolving to Monday, Monday RTH-open-to-close rejecting as out-of-window, Monday after close resolving to Tuesday using Monday close, US holidays, half-days, and DST. Doc/route guards, targeted US-short schema/doc guards, `git diff --check`, and BOM/FFFD checks should pass. Provider/live/network execution is not required for this design-only repair.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, design-only working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): accepted — valid design gap I introduced. Root cause: I copied A-share's single-`cutoff` mental model but US-short's decision cutoff is the RTH **open** (must place pre-open limit orders), which — unlike A-share's **close** cutoff — does NOT coincide with price-basis settlement, so "roll to next day immediately after open" left the Monday 09:30–16:00 ET active-session window producing a Tuesday `decision_date` whose price basis (Monday close) had not settled. Fixed `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §2.1: the live canonical window now has **both edges** — ① **start = previous trading session已收盘 (16:00 ET, incl. half-day early-close)** so the price basis is settled, ② **end = target session RTH open (9:30 ET)**; runs landing between the two edges (prev-close → target-open, incl. after-hours/overnight/weekend/holiday) resolve to that target session. **Active-session runs (a session's open→close) = dead zone → out-of-window / fail-closed**: cannot decide for the current session (open passed, entry window `first_regular_session_only` closed) nor the next (current session not closed → next session's basis = current close not settled, else a stale earlier-day close would violate the "previous closed trading day" price clock); batch-4 must NOT emit a new private packet or next-day forward-evidence decision then, and **only after the current session closes** may the resolver roll to the next trading day (basis = the just-closed session). User's window (Fri-close → Mon-open) lies entirely outside any active session → always valid, canonical=Monday; the dead zone (Mon 09:30–16:00) is outside the user window and is now explicitly defined as out-of-window for robustness. Also updated: §2.1 US-calendar bullet (DST/half-day now anchor BOTH edges — decision-end=9:30 open / roll-start=that day's close, half-day close 13:00 → roll-start advances), §2.1 price-basis bullet (window-start guarantees basis already settled, never stale), §3.5 calendar pointer (two-edge + active-session out-of-window), §18.2 batch-4 row (active-session fail-closed + injected-calendar test expectations: Fri/weekend/pre-open→Mon, Mon RTH 09:30–16:00→out-of-window reject [no packet/forward], Mon after close→Tue [basis=Mon close], US holidays→next trading day, half-day 13:00 close, DST both edges ET). Verify: doc-governance 24 OK, us_short schema suite 436 OK (design-only, code/schema untouched), residual "open→immediately roll Tuesday" framing grep = 0, `out-of-window` present in §2.1/§3.5/§18.2, `git diff --check` CRLF-only, no BOM. Boundary: design-only, no provider/live/code/真钱, US-short批3-5 + §18.0 P0 untouched, no A-share crossing. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-22): **PASS**. Verified `docs/us_short_system_design.md` now defines the canonical live window with both edges (previous session close -> target RTH open), makes active-session RTH open-to-close an explicit out-of-window / fail-closed dead zone with no packet or forward-evidence emission, and permits rolling to the next decision date only after the current session closes with that close as the price basis. Also verified section 3.5 and section 18.2 carry the same two-edge / active-session contract, and section 18.2 includes injected-calendar test expectations for Friday/weekend/pre-open, Monday active-session rejection, Monday-after-close roll, US holidays, half-days, and DST. Verification: doc/route guards 38 OK; targeted US-short schema/doc guards 66 OK; full `*us_short*` 896 OK; active design grep for the old immediate-open-roll framing clean; BOM/FFFD=0; `git diff --check` OK except CRLF warnings. No provider/live/network/batch-4 implementation was run.

### R-ASHORT-WEEKLY-CANONICAL-ASOF-LIVE-HISTORICAL-CONTRACT-DRIFT - canonical weekly cadence has conflicting live/historical predicates across resolver explicit mode and active operator docs

- Status: **resolved** (Codex `审查 FAIL` → Claude `修复` → Codex re-`审查 FAIL`(残留 same-day 注释/守护窄) → Claude `修复` round-2 2026-06-22 → Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-22; pending 用户 `提交`).
- Severity: **P2** (PIT/L3 guard contract drift; the main omitted-`-AsOf` wrapper path is directionally correct, but a new public resolver mode and active startup/operator docs encode a different predicate that can misroute future review or wrapper reuse).
- Scope reviewed: current dirty working tree for the slice `runners/resolve_canonical_asof.py`, `runners/weekly_screening.ps1`, `A-EGS/egs_main.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_resolve_canonical_asof.py`, `tests/phase6/test_egs_main_l3_guard.py`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, plus active route/operator surfaces `runners/README.md` and `docs/CURRENT.md` because the slice changes the public cadence contract. No provider/live fetch, no EGS scoring/TopN/veto/sizing change, no broker/order execution, no V14.2 rule change.
- Technical finding:
  1. The implemented wrapper/EGS/pipeline predicate is `live = as_of >= run_date`, `historical = as_of < run_date`: `weekly_screening.ps1` explicit `-AsOf` classification compares `$AsOf` to `$RunDate`, `egs_main._guard_historical_asof_l3_mode` now blocks only `as_of < run_date`, and `a_short_weekly_pipeline` allows `intraday_prior_settled` only when `--as-of >= --run-date`.
  2. The new resolver's explicit mode uses a different predicate: `resolve_canonical_asof(..., explicit_as_of=...)` classifies `historical` only when `as_of < last_settled`, and `tests/test_resolve_canonical_asof.py::test_explicit_equal_last_settled_is_live` pins `as_of == last_settled` as `live`. Direct probe: on 2026-06-20 with `last_settled=20260618`, resolver returns `{'as_of': '20260618', 'run_date': '20260620', 'mode': 'live'}`, while the wrapper predicate treats `20260618 < 20260620` as historical. That contradicts the slice claim that explicit `-AsOf` uses the pure date predicate and that all consumers share the same live/historical boundary.
  3. Active operator/route docs still teach the old same-day rule: `runners/weekly_screening.ps1` comments say M6.7/regime intraday/live behavior is `as_of==运行日`; `runners/README.md` says the regime sidecar runs only when `as_of == 运行日`; `docs/CURRENT.md` common command still says `(as_of==运行日→today)` and "必须收盘前跑". Under the new canonical weekend path, a valid live run has `as_of > run_date`, so these active surfaces are now false.
- Why material: the changed slice is a cadence / PIT guard change, not a cosmetic refactor. The exact live/historical predicate controls default `l3=today`, M6.7 price-freshness tolerance, regime/overlay forward sidecars, and historical replay safeguards. A public resolver/test that marks a past settled decision date as `live`, plus startup/operator docs that still say only same-day is live, can lead a future implementer or reviewer to reintroduce the old guard or to consume resolver `mode` incorrectly.
- Required repair: choose one narrow repair package and keep behavior boundaries unchanged. Preferred: remove or neutralize the resolver's explicit `--as-of` classification path because `weekly_screening.ps1` deliberately does not call it for explicit `-AsOf`; OR change resolver explicit mode to the same `as_of < run_date` predicate used by the wrapper/EGS/pipeline. In either case update `tests/test_resolve_canonical_asof.py` so a weekend explicit last-settled date is historical (or explicit resolver mode is unsupported), and keep omitted-`-AsOf` canonical behavior unchanged. Also update active comments/route docs in `weekly_screening.ps1`, `runners/README.md`, and `docs/CURRENT.md` to say "live = not historical / `as_of >= run_date` (including prospective canonical)" instead of `as_of == 运行日`, and strengthen the existing route-doc guard test so the old same-day-only wording cannot recur on active cadence surfaces.
- Verification expected: resolver tests prove omitted canonical weekend/holiday behavior still resolves to the upcoming trading day; explicit-mode test proves the predicate no longer disagrees with the wrapper, or that explicit mode is not exposed by the resolver; weekly wrapper guardrails still pass; direct M6.7 probe still shows `run_date < as_of` passes `accept_prior_settled_date` and `run_date > as_of` fails; route-doc/SESSION_LOG guards pass; grep for active `as_of==运行日` / `as_of == 运行日` / same-day-only cadence wording is clean except clearly historical archived prose.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged both contradictions valid + in-scope + accepted — finding 2 is a real predicate-drift bug I introduced (resolver explicit mode `as_of < last_settled` disagrees with the `as_of < run_date` contract used by wrapper/EGS/pipeline; my own `test_explicit_equal_last_settled_is_live` locked the wrong boundary), finding 3 is the doc B-ripple of a behavior change. Took Codex's **preferred** package — **removed the resolver's explicit-`--as-of` classification path entirely** (it was vestigial: `weekly_screening.ps1` deliberately does explicit-`-AsOf` classification in pure PowerShell via `as_of < run_date`, never calling the resolver for it; keeping a second predicate was the drift surface). `resolve_canonical_asof()` now takes no `explicit_as_of`, returns only `{as_of, run_date, last_settled}` (no `mode` — canonical is always live by construction; ps1 omitted-branch sets `$IsHistoricalAsOf=$false`), and `main()` no longer accepts `--as-of` (argparse rejects it). So the ONLY live/historical predicate left anywhere is `as_of < run_date` (egs guard, pipeline price-freshness, ps1 explicit branch). Tests: deleted the 5 explicit-mode tests, dropped `mode` assertions from canonical tests, added `test_output_has_no_mode_field` + `test_main_does_not_accept_explicit_asof` (proves explicit mode is not exposed). Docs: updated `weekly_screening.ps1` Stage-4/5 comments, `runners/README.md` regime line, `docs/CURRENT.md` cadence command block from `as_of==运行日` → `live = as_of >= 运行日 (含前瞻 canonical) / historical = as_of < 运行日`; added active-cadence-surface anti-recurrence guard `tests/phase6/test_weekly_screening_guardrails.py::test_active_cadence_surfaces_no_same_day_only_wording` (forbids `as_of==运行日`/`as_of == 运行日` on ps1/README/CURRENT + pins the live-predicate doc; historical §0 deltas use other prose, not false-flagged). Verify: resolver 16 OK, egs l3 guard 5 OK, 3 intraday/freshness OK, phase6 65 OK (guardrails incl. new guard), doc-governance 24 OK, full weekly_pipeline 435 OK (private ratchet sidecar isolated then restored); ps1 PARSE OK; grep `as_of==运行日`/`as_of == 运行日` on active surfaces = 0; no `explicit_as_of`/`mode` field left in resolver; BOM 0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF. Boundary unchanged: research-only/advisory, A股主板, no EGS scoring/TopN/veto/sizing/provider/broker, V14.2 frozen — pure cadence. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

However, active modified surfaces still teach the old same-day-only contract: `runners/weekly_screening.ps1` top stage summary still says regime and overlay **只在实盘当天跑** (lines 11 and 14), its Stage 6 comment repeats **只在实盘当天跑** (line 350), and `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py::_fetch_price_series` still says `accept_prior_settled_date` is passed only when ``--run-date == --as-of`` (line 2305). ### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-PRICE-DESPIKE-TIED-LONG-SHADOW - de-spike compared the extreme to the single 2nd-ordered value, so 2+ bars wicking to the SAME extreme survived as 'strong'

- Status: **resolved** (committed `4c6c31d3`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22). Was Round B Cut 2 — the LAST converged-review item; this commit closes the entire batch-2 review (Round A 7 + Round B 2).
- Severity: **P2** (price-geometry design-hole; was `cc_review_v2 §4.1`).
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` §4.1 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §4.1. The user explicitly authorized my recommended disposition ("4.1 按你建议执行" = deviate from the A-share mirror + add a §6 deviation note).
- Scope reviewed/repaired: `engine/us_short_price_engine.py::effective_support` + `::effective_resistance` (+ their docstrings, the `SR_SPIKE_ATR` comment, and the module docstring) + `tests/test_us_short_price_engine.py` + the `docs/README.md` price route row + `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §6 (line 196). No provider/live/A-share/batch3.
- Technical finding: `effective_support` used `second_low = sorted(lows)[1]` and `effective_resistance` used `second_high = sorted(highs)[-2]` (the single 2nd-ORDERED value). When 2+ bars share the extreme (TIED long shadows), the 2nd-ordered value EQUALS the extreme → diff 0 → `0 > SR_SPIKE_ATR×ATR` is False → the multi-bar wick survives and is marked `strong`. §6 itself notes US long shadows are more extreme (no daily limit) and can repeat across bars — exactly the case the single-2nd-value mirror missed. The `effective_resistance` value feeds the new-entry t1/RR numerator AND the holding trailing-stop basis, so a surviving tied wick distorts both entry sizing and exit levels.
- Disposition (user-authorized "按你建议执行" — deviate from the A-short mirror): compare the extreme against the NEAREST STRICTLY-DIFFERENT value (`next_low = min(lo for lo in lows if lo > raw_low)` / `next_high = max(hi for hi in highs if hi < raw_high)`), so 2+ bars wicking to the same extreme are still de-spiked. The `SR_SPIKE_ATR` (§13 #24) threshold is UNCHANGED. Single-wick, backed, flat-window, and fallback cases are all unchanged (verified). This is a deliberate US-short refinement of the A-short `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py` single-2nd-value de-spike; the A-share engine is a DIFFERENT lane and was NOT touched (no A-share crossing) — the divergence is documented.
- Frozen-design note (user-authorized): added a `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §6 (line 196) refinement — "取次值" → "取最近的非并列值 (US-short 刻意比 A 股 phase5「取单一次值」更稳健 … §13 #24 倍数不变)" — per the user's explicit decision to deviate. All other §6 rules + the §13 #24 multiplier are unchanged.
- Verify: probes — support tied `[90,90,100×18]` → (100, 'weak', 90) [was (90,'strong')]; single `[90,100×19]` → (100,'weak') unchanged; backed `[99,100×19]` → (99,'strong') unchanged; resistance tied `[110,110,100×18]` → (100,'weak',110). price_engine 34 OK (incl 2 new tied-shadow tests); full us_short lane 896 OK (894 + 2), zero regression. Doc-drift proof: grep `2nd value` / `取次值` / `2nd-lowest` / `second_low` across active surfaces → 0 stale us_short teaching surface (the only hits are the new docstrings/test explaining the refinement, the untouched A-share engine [different lane], and historical register prose).
- Codex review closure (2026-06-22): PASS. Confirmed tied long shadows are de-spiked for support + resistance, single-wick / backed / flat-window / fallback cases remain unchanged, §6 + README + docstrings document the user-authorized US-short refinement, §13 #24 multiplier remains unchanged, and the A-share engine is untouched. Verification: price_engine 34 OK; all `*us_short*` 896 OK; schema `*us_short*` 436 OK; doc/route 38 OK; direct tied/single/backed/flat/fallback probes passed; active stale de-spike grep clean except the untouched A-share lane and historical prose. **This is the LAST converged batch-2 review item — its commit closes the entire Round A + Round B review.**

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-PRIVATEPATH-RELATIVE-CWD-BYPASS - the §18.0 P0 private-path guard resolves a relative path against the CWD, not ROOT, so a non-root-CWD relative path bypasses the in-repo check

- Status: **resolved** (committed `81341a0f`, Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-22). The related CLI doc/help drift `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-PRIVATEPATH-CLI-RELATIVE-OUTPUT-DOC-DRIFT` is also resolved in this closeout.
- Severity: **P2** (latent; no git-commit leak — a bypassed path lands OUTSIDE the repo — but a privacy-sensitive file [real holdings, for the converter] can land in an unintended CWD-relative location, and the in-repo gitignore proof is silently skipped).
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` R7 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §5.5 / §P2-7.
- Scope reviewed/repaired (whole-class sweep): `engine/us_short_private_paths.py::reject_nonprivate_output_path` (the named §18.0 P0 helper) AND its live mirror `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py::_reject_nonprivate_account_output_path` (the real-holdings account_state writer — same bug, reachable via a relative `--out`), plus both test files + the README private_paths route row. No provider/live/A-share/batch3.
- Technical finding:
  - Both guards did `p = Path(out_path).resolve()`, which resolves a RELATIVE out_path against the process CWD (not ROOT). From a non-root CWD a relative path resolves OUTSIDE the repo → `p.relative_to(ROOT)` raises → the "outside the repo → OK (external private)" branch returns, skipping `git check-ignore` entirely. The guard's correctness silently depended on an unstated "caller passes an absolute path / CWD == repo root" precondition.
  - The converter is the higher-stakes case: a relative `--out` reaches the guard live (`out_path = Path(args.out)` is NOT resolved before the guard), so a user running it from a non-root CWD writes real holdings to an unintended location.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): both guards now reject a non-absolute path up front — `if not Path(out_path).is_absolute(): raise PrivatePathError/ConvertError(...)` — before `.resolve()`. A relative / CWD-dependent path is refused (privacy unprovable); callers must pass an ABSOLUTE path (an external private location, or an in-repo path built from `ROOT`). `is_absolute()` is platform-correct (a Windows drive-relative `/foo` is also refused). Updated both guard docstrings (Decision blocks) + the README private_paths route row to list the new relative-refusal case (proactive doc sync, per the step-3/step-5 doc-drift lessons; grep of README/design/docstrings/test-docstrings shows no surface asserts "accepts relative").
- Verify: both guard suites 82 OK (incl 3 new: private_paths relative-refused + relative-refused-before-git; converter relative-refused); full us_short lane 892 OK (889 + 3), zero regression; probes confirm relative → refused, absolute-gitignored → still OK, outside-repo absolute → still OK for both. No automated caller passes a relative `--out` (grep: only the CLI + tests, which use absolute paths) → no breakage.
- Class-coverage note (out-of-lane, flagged, NOT fixed): the A-share mirror `runners/a_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py` very likely has the same `Path(out_path).resolve()` relative-CWD pattern. It is a DIFFERENT lane (A-share) — deliberately NOT touched in this US-short cut (no A-share crossing). Flagged here for a separate A-short-lane review/decision; not silently dropped.
- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-22): PASS. Confirmed both US-short guards refuse a relative path before any git/outside-repo branch and still allow absolute gitignored / external paths. The prior active converter CLI usage/help drift is now resolved in `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-PRIVATEPATH-CLI-RELATIVE-OUTPUT-DOC-DRIFT`. Remaining Round A item (main-design doc drift) + Round B stay queued; closure pending 用户 `提交`.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-ACTIONRANK-GROUP1-SURVIVAL-ORDER - action_rank group-1 (holding exits) ordered by selection_rank only, so a 止盈减仓 outranks a 止损清仓

- Status: **resolved** (committed `6adcd378`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22). Was in_progress for Round A step 5 sub-fix a of the converged batch-2 review.
- Severity: **P2**.
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` R6 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §3.1 / §P2-5. (Codex asked for the two action_rank fixes to be tracked + tested SEPARATELY — this is the survival-order half; the float-rank half is `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-ACTIONRANK-FLOAT-SELECTION-RANK`.)
- Scope reviewed/repaired: `engine/us_short_action_rank.py::rank_actions` (within-group-1 sub-order) + `tests/test_us_short_action_rank.py::Group1SurvivalOrderTests` + the `docs/README.md` action_rank route row. No provider/live/A-share/batch3.
- Technical finding:
  - `rank_actions` sorted EVERY group by `(group, selection_rank, index)`. But §9 (design line 248) assigns `selection_rank` to GROUP-2 ordering; a group-1 holding exit (止损/事件清仓) usually carries no selection_rank → `math.inf` → sorts LAST within group 1.
  - Trace: `rank_actions([{"final_action":"减仓","selection_rank":1}, {"final_action":"清仓-止损"}])` → 减仓 got action_rank 1, 清仓-止损 got 2 — a loss-preventing stop-clear ranked BEHIND a profit-side 减仓 (both still ahead of any new buy, so P2 not P1, but it violates the within-group survival order §9 exists to protect).
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): added a within-group-1 survival sub-order `_GROUP1_EXIT_PRIORITY` (止损/事件清仓 = 0 → 减仓 = 1 → 止盈清仓 = 2), applied as `(group, survival, selection_rank, index)`. It is a CONSTANT (0) for groups 2-5, so their existing selection_rank order is unchanged; only inside group 1 does survival precede selection_rank. Updated the rank_actions docstring + README route row to match (route-doc synced proactively, per the step-3 lesson).
  - **In-slice design choice (flagged for review)**: a 减仓's driver (stop- vs profit-driven) is not carried on `final_action`, so all 减仓 sit in the MIDDLE tier (after the unambiguous survival clears, before the pure 止盈清仓). The safety property — a 止损/事件清仓 never sorts behind a 减仓 or 止盈清仓 — holds regardless. If the user wants 减仓 sub-typed (stop-driven 减仓 = tier 0), that needs a new row field + design decision.
- Verify: `rank_actions([减仓 rank1, 清仓-止损])` → 清仓-止损 action_rank 1 (was 2); survival exits precede 减仓 precede 止盈清仓; same-tier still breaks by selection_rank; groups 2-5 unchanged. action_rank 17 OK (incl 3 new survival-order tests); full us_short lane 889 OK, zero regression.
- Closure: Codex `审查` confirms a 止损/事件清仓 outranks a 止盈减仓/止盈清仓 within group 1 and groups 2-5 are unchanged, then 用户 `提交`. (The 减仓-middle-tier design choice is submitted for the user's/Codex's judgment.)
- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-22): PASS. Confirmed group 1 now sorts by survival tier before rank (`清仓-止损` / `清仓-事件` before `减仓` before `清仓-止盈`), same-tier group-1 rows still use `selection_rank`, and groups 2-5 keep their selection-rank order. The `减仓` middle tier is accepted for this cut because `final_action` carries no stop-vs-profit driver; changing that would require a future design/field decision. Verified by target tests, full US-short tests, and direct probes. No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/batch3 path was run.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-ACTIONRANK-FLOAT-SELECTION-RANK - action_rank `_rank_value` rejects integer-valued floats, stricter than the sibling engines

- Status: **resolved** (committed `6adcd378`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22). Was in_progress for Round A step 5 sub-fix b of the converged batch-2 review.
- Severity: **P2** (Codex note: downgradeable to P3 if a future schema mandates an integer `selection_rank`; no such strong schema gate exists today → P2).
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` R6 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §P2-6. (The separate float-rank half of the two action_rank fixes; survival-order half = `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-ACTIONRANK-GROUP1-SURVIVAL-ORDER`.)
- Scope reviewed/repaired: `engine/us_short_action_rank.py::_rank_value` + `tests/test_us_short_action_rank.py::FloatSelectionRankTests` + the README selection_rank wording. No provider/live/A-share/batch3.
- Technical finding:
  - `_rank_value` used `not isinstance(x, int)` → a float `selection_rank` (`1.0` from JSON / numpy / upstream float math) → None → `math.inf` → the STRONGEST buy sorts LAST within group 2. Stricter than the sibling engines' `_finite_number` (which accepts int OR float); `selection_rank` has no typed schema gate, so a float is a realistic upstream shape.
  - Trace: `rank_actions([{"final_action":"建仓","selection_rank":1.0}, {...:2}, {...:3}])` → the rank-1.0 row sorted LAST. Group-internal only (no cross-group effect) → P2.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): `_rank_value` now accepts an integer-VALUED finite float (`1.0` → `1`) while still rejecting a non-integer float (`1.5`), bool, NaN/Inf, string, or `< 1` → None (sorts last). Parity with the sibling numeric handling; a non-integer / malformed rank is still fail-closed to last-within-group.
- Verify: `selection_rank=1.0/2.0/3.0` → ranks 1/2/3 (was last); `1.5 / True / NaN / "1"` → sorts last. action_rank 17 OK (incl 2 new float-rank tests); full us_short lane 889 OK, zero regression.
- Closure: Codex `审查` confirms an integer-valued float ranks correctly and a non-integer / bool / string still sorts last, then 用户 `提交`. Remaining Round A items (private_paths / main-design doc drift) + Round B stay queued.
- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-22): PASS. Confirmed `_rank_value` accepts finite integer-valued floats (`1.0` -> `1`) and still rejects bool, non-integer float, NaN/Inf, string, `None`, and values `< 1` so malformed ranks sink within their rank tier. Verified by target tests, full US-short tests, schema tests, and direct probes. No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/batch3 path was run.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-THEMELIFECYCLE-CONFIRM-COUNT-UNVALIDATED - theme_lifecycle confirm_count is consumed unvalidated, so a bool/float can force a single-round upgrade

- Status: **resolved** (committed `f620468d`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22). Was in_progress for Round A step 4. (NB: commit `f620468d`'s inline message note "Codex 审查 was NOT run" is ERRONEOUS — Codex did review and PASS this cut before commit, per the SESSION_LOG PASS entry + the Codex re-review closure below; the note came from a stale pre-Codex read at flag-time that was not re-checked right before commit.)
- Severity: **P2**.
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` R5 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §P2 (action 5.7).
- Scope reviewed/repaired: `engine/us_short_theme_lifecycle.py::next_theme_lifecycle_state` + `tests/test_us_short_theme_lifecycle.py`. No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/batch3.
- Technical finding:
  - `next_theme_lifecycle_state` HARD-validates the sibling `upgrade_confirm_runs` (int, not bool, ≥2 → ValueError) but consumed `confirm_count` (the consecutive-confirmation streak) UNVALIDATED at `c = confirm_count + 1`.
  - Trace: `next_theme_lifecycle_state("provisional_active", confirming=True, confirm_count=True)` → `True + 1 = 2 ≥ upgrade_confirm_runs(2)` → `("confirmed_active", 0)` — a SINGLE-round upgrade, bypassing the §13 #30 up-slow anti-chatter (consecutive confirmations). `confirm_count=1.5` similarly upgrades; a string `confirm_count` would raise a bare TypeError at `+1`.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): validate `confirm_count` with the SAME strict-int discipline as `upgrade_confirm_runs` — a non-negative int, NOT a bool; bool / non-int / negative → ValueError (fail closed, consistent with the engine's existing raise-on-bad-prior_state / raise-on-bad-upgrade_confirm_runs contract). ### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-THEMEHEAT-PERSISTENCE-MULT-AMPLIFY - theme_heat persistence_mult is lower-clamped only, so an out-of-range value AMPLIFIES the 0-100 score

- Status: **resolved** (committed `8c14e0e8`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22 — runtime + the route-doc drift `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-THEMEHEAT-ROUTEDOC-FORMULA-DRIFT`). Was open P2.
- Severity: **P2**.
- Source: converged batch-2 review — Codex `review_v2.md` R4 + Claude `cc_review_v2.md` §P2-3.
- Scope reviewed/repaired: `engine/us_short_theme_heat.py::continuous_theme_score` (+ the shared `_finite`) and `engine/us_short_overextension.py::_finite`, plus their tests. No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/batch3.
- Technical finding:
  - `continuous_theme_score` returned `heat × max(pm, persistence_floor) × clamp(fit_mult)`. The `max(pm, floor)` only LOWER-clamps persistence_mult, but §4.3 defines it as a [0,1] discount. An out-of-range pm AMPLIFIES the 0-100 block score: `continuous_theme_score(80.0, persistence_mult=5.0, fit_mult=1.0, gate_passed=True)` → 400.0 (asymmetric with fit_mult, already `max(0, min(1, fm))`).
  - Compounded by the lenient `_finite` (`R-USSHORT-BATCH2-LENIENT-FINITE-OVEREXTENSION-THEMEHEAT-HYGIENE`): `pm="5"` PARSED (`float("5")=5.0`) AND amplified.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-22, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): double-clamp persistence_mult → `max(min(pm, 1.0), persistence_floor)` (floor AND ceil 1.0) so an out-of-range value can only DISCOUNT, never amplify; the post-gate floor still protects a fresh high-heat theme. Folded the related strict-`_finite` fix (theme_heat + overextension) into the same cut (see `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-LENIENT-FINITE-OVEREXTENSION-THEMEHEAT-HYGIENE`), closing the parse+amplify compound.
- Verify: `continuous_theme_score(80, 5.0, 1.0, gate=True)` → 80.0 (was 400); pm=0.1 → 24.0 (floor still applies); pm="5"/True → 0.0 (strict finite). theme_heat + overextension 30 OK (incl 3 new clamp/finite tests); full us_short lane 883 OK (880 + 3), zero regression. `_finite` class-coverage check: only theme_heat + overextension had the lenient score-field parse; `regime.classify_vix` string-parse is intentional + tested ("18"→震荡), `price_engine` tick helpers have safe fallbacks — both out of this finding's scope.
- Codex runtime re-review closure (2026-06-22): PASS for code behavior. Confirmed `persistence_mult` cannot amplify (`pm=5` and `pm=100` cap to the raw heat contribution), the floor still applies (`pm=0.1` → floor 0.30), and bool / numeric-string heat / multiplier inputs fail closed to 0. Verified: theme_heat + overextension 30 OK; all `*us_short*` tests 883 OK; schema `*us_short*` tests 436 OK; doc-governance / route guards 38 OK; direct probes passed; `git diff --check` only LF/CRLF warnings; no BOM. Separate P3 doc drift `R-USSHORT-BATCH2-THEMEHEAT-ROUTEDOC-FORMULA-DRIFT` blocks clean PASS / commit until repaired. Remaining Round A items (theme_lifecycle confirm_count / action_rank / private_paths / main-design doc drift; + Round B design decisions) stay queued.

- Status: **resolved** (committed `18cd7494`, Codex `审查 PASS` 2026-06-22).
