### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-ORTHO-PERFECT-OVERLAP-BOOST-GAP - US-short industry-theme orthogonal residual turns perfect overlap into max score

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was open P1 (Codex `审查 FAIL` 2026-06-21).
- Severity: **P1**.
- Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short batch2 seventh slice (`engine/us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py`, `tests/test_us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py`, plus `docs/README.md` / `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`). No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py::orthogonalize_industry_on_theme` computes OLS residuals, then `_percentile_rank_0_100` maps each residual to `(count <= value) / n * 100`. When `industry_heat_score` is perfectly explained by `theme_heat_score`, every residual is `0`, so every row ties at the top percentile and receives `100.0`.
  - Independent probe: rows `(theme, industry) = (10,20),(20,40),(30,60),(40,80)` returned `[100.0, 100.0, 100.0, 100.0]`.
  - The current test `test_perfectly_explained_industry_has_no_orthogonal_signal` asserts that all-100 output, so the test suite locks in the opposite of the stated "no orthogonal signal" intent.
  - `_safe_min_paired` also permits integer `min_paired=2`, despite the module-level invariant `MIN_PAIRED = 3` and the docs/tests saying fewer than 3 paired rows degenerates. Probe: two paired rows returned `[50.0, 100.0]` by default but `[100.0, 100.0]` when `min_paired=2`.
- Why this is material: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 and §18.1 #22 require `industry_heat` and `theme_heat` overlap to be counted once. This slice is the future input to the §4.2 35% theme/industry block. If perfect overlap is emitted as max orthogonal residual, the later residual coefficient can add industry heat even when theme already explains it, or at least create a high constant residual boost where there is no separable industry information.
- Required repair:
  1. After OLS, detect zero / near-zero residual dispersion and return a non-boosting orthogonal industry value for those paired rows. Acceptable shapes include all `0.0`, or another explicitly documented neutral/non-boost convention, but not all `100.0` / max residual.
  2. Replace the current perfect-fit test so it proves "perfectly explained industry does not produce a max orthogonal residual boost"; keep positive controls where a genuine industry outlier receives the highest residual percentile.
  3. Tighten or explicitly justify `min_paired`: if `MIN_PAIRED=3` is the invariant, integer `2` must fall back to the default or be rejected; if lower thresholds are intentionally allowed, document that as calibration behavior and add tests showing it is not mistaken for the default fail-closed path.
  4. Keep the repair narrow: no 35%-block directional assembly, no sizing/action_rank/batch3 renderer/validator, no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker work, no weight calibration, and no unrelated refactor.
- Evidence collected by Codex: target tests passed (`tests.test_us_short_theme_orthogonalize`: 10 OK); US-short discover passed (`tests -p '*us_short*'`: 650 OK); US-short schema passed (408 OK); doc-governance/route guards passed (38 OK); `git diff --check` returned 0 with CRLF warnings only. Independent probes reproduced perfect-overlap `[100,100,100,100]` and `min_paired=2` bypassing the default `<3` degenerate path.
- Closure requires Claude `修复` to make perfect-overlap residual output non-boosting with adversarial tests, decide/pin the `min_paired` lower-bound behavior, then Codex re-`审查` to confirm genuine outliers still rank high, degenerate fallback still returns industry percentile, malformed rows still fail closed, and no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path was introduced.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged both findings valid + accepted. **Finding 1 was a real semantic bug AND a self-review failure**: perfect industry-on-theme overlap produced all-100 (max boost) instead of "no separable signal", and my own test locked that wrong output in as "correct" — I asserted what the code produced instead of what §4.3 intends (overlap counted ONCE → perfect overlap → 0). Fixed in `engine/us_short_theme_orthogonalize.py`: after OLS, if the residual dispersion is ~zero (`_variance(resid) < 1e-9`) the paired rows get a non-boosting `0.0` (overlap counted once, NOT a max-percentile boost); the genuine-outlier path is unchanged (real residual dispersion → percentile, the outlier still tops at 100). **Finding 2 (min_paired floor)**: `_safe_min_paired` now requires `>= MIN_PAIRED` (3) — the hard floor (2 points always fit a line perfectly, so a lower threshold is meaningless); `min_paired=2` (or any int < 3) falls back to 3 → 2 paired rows degenerate to the industry percentile, never a meaningless 2-point regression; a caller may still RAISE it (calibration). Tests: replaced the wrong-locking perfect-fit test with `test_perfectly_explained_industry_is_non_boosting_zero` (all 0.0); strengthened the min_paired test to cover int 2 → default; added `test_min_paired_two_does_not_regress_two_points` ([50,100] degenerate) and `test_min_paired_can_be_raised_for_calibration` (min_paired=5 degenerates a 4-paired pool); the genuine-outlier / degenerate-fallback / malformed-row controls are unchanged + still pass. Verify: theme-orthogonalize target 12 OK; tests/ us_short 652 OK + tests/schema 408 OK (zero regression); independent probe confirms perfect overlap → [0,0,0,0] and min_paired=2 → [50,100] degenerate; BOM=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; doc-governance/route 38 OK. No 35%-block directional assembly / sizing / action_rank / batch3 / provider / live / DataHub / A-share / broker; no weight calibration. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-21): PASS. Re-reviewed the current dirty tree, reran the target theme-orthogonalize tests (12 OK), `tests -p '*us_short*'` discover (652 OK), `tests/schema -p '*us_short*'` discover (408 OK), and doc-governance/route guards (38 OK). Independent probes confirmed perfect industry/theme overlap returns `[0,0,0,0]`, `min_paired=2` falls back to the 3-row floor and returns the degenerate industry percentile `[50,100]`, genuine residual outliers still rank highest, zero-theme-variance fallback still returns industry percentile, industry-only rows stay `None` in regression mode, malformed rows still fail closed, and no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path was run.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-CORESCORE-NEUTRAL-BLOCK-BAD-SHAPE-GAP - US-short core_score neutral fallback parameter can crash or contaminate scoring

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was open P1 (Codex `审查 FAIL` 2026-06-21).
- Severity: **P1**.
- Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short batch2 sixth slice (`engine/us_short_core_score.py`, `tests/test_us_short_core_score.py`, plus `docs/README.md` / `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`). No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_core_score.py::core_score` validates real block values and `risk_downgrade_points` with `_finite_number`, but the public `neutral_block` fallback parameter is assigned directly to any missing / malformed block and then multiplied into the weighted sum.
  - Independent probes reproduced multiple bad-shape outcomes when a block is missing: `neutral_block="50"` raises `TypeError`; `neutral_block=None` raises `TypeError`; `neutral_block=float("nan")` stores `nan` in `blocks_used` and relies on final `max()` behavior to emit `0.0`; `neutral_block=float("inf")` emits `core_score=inf`; `neutral_block=1000.0` emits `core_score=303.0`; `neutral_block=True/False` is accepted as `1/0`-like fallback. These values bypass the stated whole-class strict numeric policy.
  - Existing tests cover malformed blocks, malformed `risk_downgrade_points`, unknown profile, non-dict blocks, copy-safe weights, and missing-block non-renormalization, but they do not adversarially test malformed / out-of-range `neutral_block`.
- Why this is material: `core_score` is the §4.2 ranking primitive that §8 sizing and §9 action_rank will consume. The slice explicitly claims every public input is fail-closed and that a missing block scores neutral without re-normalizing the other weights. An unvalidated fallback can crash scoring, produce NaN/Inf, or inflate missing-data rows above the intended 0-100 scoring domain, which can contaminate Top15 ranking once downstream consumers wire this function.
- Required repair:
  1. Validate `neutral_block` at the same API boundary as other numeric public inputs. Bad shapes (`str`, `bool`, `None`, NaN, Inf) must not crash, propagate, or become live fallback values.
  2. Ensure the neutral fallback cannot leave the 0-100 block domain or silently inflate missing blocks. Acceptable behavior: reject invalid/out-of-domain overrides loudly, or fail closed to the frozen `NEUTRAL_BLOCK` / clamped block-domain value, but the behavior must be deliberate and tested.
  3. Add adversarial tests for malformed `neutral_block` values (`"50"`, `True`, `False`, `None`, NaN, Inf) and out-of-domain numeric values (negative / very large), plus positive controls for the normal missing-block 50 behavior and any intentionally allowed numeric override.
  4. Keep the repair narrow: no cross-sectional industry-theme orthogonalization, no sizing/action_rank/batch3 renderer/validator, no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker work, no weight calibration, and no unrelated refactor.
- Evidence collected by Codex: target tests passed (`tests.test_us_short_core_score`: 14 OK); US-short discover passed (`tests -p '*us_short*'`: 638 OK); US-short schema passed (408 OK); doc-governance/route guards passed (38 OK); `git diff --check` returned 0 with CRLF warnings only. Independent probes reproduced `neutral_block` crash / NaN / Inf / score-boost behavior. Search of the new core-score files found no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path.
- Closure requires Claude `修复` to validate or reject the `neutral_block` fallback with tests, then Codex re-`审查` to confirm malformed fallback values cannot crash, emit NaN/Inf, or inflate scores, while normal weights, missing-block neutral behavior, no-renormalization, copy-safe profile weights, and risk_downgrade subtraction remain intact.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged valid + accepted (in-scope, material — same whole-class input-validation class, and an honest miss: I validated the `blocks` values + `risk_downgrade_points` but overlooked the `neutral_block` fallback PARAMETER, even right after writing the `whole-class-input-validation-sweep` memory — the audit must cover EVERY parameter incl. default/config fallbacks, not just the data args). Fixed narrowly in `engine/us_short_core_score.py` + its tests: `core_score` now validates `neutral_block` at the same boundary — `_finite_number` (rejects bool + numeric string) plus a 0-100 domain check, so a malformed (`"50"` / None / bool / NaN / Inf) or out-of-domain (`1000` / `-10`) override fails closed to the frozen `NEUTRAL_BLOCK` (50) instead of crashing, propagating NaN/Inf, or inflating a missing-data row above the scoring domain; a legitimate in-domain numeric override (e.g. 40) still applies. Every parameter of both public functions is now validated (`blocks` dict + values, `profile` raises-on-unknown, `risk_downgrade_points`, `neutral_block`). Tests: added `NeutralBlockValidationTests` (malformed + out-of-domain neutral_block → frozen 50, score stays in 0-100; legitimate 40 override positive control); normal weights / missing-block neutral / no-renormalization / copy-safe / risk_downgrade tests unchanged + still pass. Verify: core-score target 16 OK (+2); tests/ us_short 640 OK + tests/schema 408 OK (zero regression); independent probe confirms neutral_block="50" no crash, Inf/1000 → core_score 65.5 (in domain), legitimate 40 applies; BOM=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; doc-governance/route 38 OK. No orthogonalization / sizing / action_rank / batch3 / provider / live / DataHub / A-share / broker; no weight calibration. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.
- Codex re-review closure (2026-06-21): PASS. Re-reviewed the current dirty tree, reran core-score target tests (16 OK), `tests -p '*us_short*'` discover (640 OK), `tests/schema -p '*us_short*'` discover (408 OK), and doc-governance/route guards (38 OK). Independent probes confirmed malformed / bool / non-finite / out-of-domain `neutral_block` values fall back to the frozen 50 without crash, NaN/Inf, or score inflation; legitimate in-domain overrides 0/40/100 still apply; malformed blocks and `risk_downgrade_points` still fail closed; all scoring profiles load from the frozen preset; returned profile weights remain copy-safe; unknown profiles raise; and no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path was run.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-RISK-DOWNGRADE-BAD-SHAPE-SOFT-SIGNAL-GAP - US-short risk_downgrade soft-signal API treats malformed flags/events as valid penalties or invalid score values

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was open P1 across 3 Codex FAIL rounds (original bad-shape → residual margin-override → residual return-input bool), now closed by a whole-class public-input-validation sweep.
- Severity: **P1**.
- Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short batch2 fifth slice (`engine/us_short_risk_downgrade.py`, `tests/test_us_short_risk_downgrade.py`, plus `docs/README.md` / `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`). No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_risk_downgrade.py::current_good_data_bad_reaction_event` treats any truthy `earnings_beat` value as a confirmed beat. Codex probes showed `earnings_beat="False"` and `earnings_beat="unknown"` both returned `{"is_event": True, "soft_penalty": 10.0}` when returns otherwise matched the downgrade case.
  - `engine/us_short_risk_downgrade.py::risk_downgrade` treats any truthy `analyst_collective_downgrade` value as a downgrade. Probe: `analyst_collective_downgrade="False"` produced an 8-point analyst penalty.
  - `risk_downgrade` trusts caller-supplied `current_event` fields without validating the shape or numeric value. Probes: `{"is_event": "False", "soft_penalty": 10}` counted as a 10-point penalty; `{"is_event": True, "soft_penalty": "10"}` raised `TypeError`; `soft_penalty=-100.0` made `points=-100.0` (a score boost, the opposite of a downgrade); `NaN` / `Inf` propagated into final points.
  - `current_good_data_bad_reaction_event` also uses `exempt_margin` directly. Bad overrides such as string / `None` raised `TypeError`, while negative / non-finite margins can invert or degrade the exemption gate. The current tests cover finite return values and history bad inputs, but not these same-class public-API bad-shape paths.
- Why this is material: `risk_downgrade` is a §4.2 scoring primitive that future `core_score` will subtract before ranking Top15. A malformed upstream parser value or event object can fabricate a soft penalty, produce NaN/Inf, crash scoring, or turn a risk downgrade into a score boost. The slice is not yet wired to core_score, but this is the exact point where the reusable decision-engine contract must fail closed before downstream consumers rely on it.
- Required repair:
  1. Make boolean signal gates exact and fail-closed: `earnings_beat` and `analyst_collective_downgrade` must only trigger on explicit `True` (or another strictly validated internal representation); truthy strings / integers / unknown values must not become live downgrade signals.
  2. Validate `current_event` shape at the API boundary. It must not count truthy non-bool `is_event`, non-finite / non-numeric / negative `soft_penalty`, or any malformed object in a way that produces a penalty, NaN/Inf, negative points, or uncaught TypeError. Either reject bad event objects loudly or fail closed to zero, but the behavior must be deliberate and tested.
  3. Validate threshold overrides such as `exempt_margin` before arithmetic; bad, negative, or non-finite values must fail closed or be rejected, not crash or weaken the relative-exemption gate.
  4. Add adversarial tests for the full bad-shape class: truthy-string `earnings_beat`, truthy-string / numeric analyst flag, truthy-string `is_event`, string / `None` / negative / NaN / Inf event penalties, and bad `exempt_margin` values, plus positive controls for the legitimate `True` signals and existing boundary/exemption cases.
  5. Keep the repair narrow: no hard-veto escalation, no core_score assembly, no sizing/action_rank/batch3 renderer/validator, no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker work, and no threshold calibration beyond safe input validation.
- Evidence collected by Codex: target tests passed (`tests.test_us_short_risk_downgrade`: 13 OK); US-short discover passed (`tests -p '*us_short*'`: 614 OK); US-short schema passed (408 OK); doc-governance/route guards passed (38 OK); `git diff --check` returned 0 with CRLF warnings only. Independent probes reproduced truthy-string beat/analyst penalties, malformed current-event penalties/crashes/negative points/NaN/Inf, and bad margin errors/inversion risk.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-LIFECYCLE-MUTABLE-EFFECT-UPGRADE-GUARD-GAP - US-short batch2 lifecycle engine exposes mutable frozen effects and lets up-slow confirmation be bypassed

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was open P1 (Codex `review FAIL` 2026-06-21).
- Severity: **P1**.
- Scope reviewed: current dirty working tree US-short batch2 third slice (`engine/us_short_theme_lifecycle.py`, `engine/us_short_overextension.py`, `tests/test_us_short_theme_lifecycle.py`, `tests/test_us_short_overextension.py`, plus `docs/README.md` / `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`). No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_theme_lifecycle.py::lifecycle_effects` returns `TRANSITION_ACTIONS[state]` directly from the module-level governance table. A caller can mutate the returned nested dict and thereby mutate the supposedly frozen transition-action table for the rest of the process. Codex probe: `eff = lifecycle_effects("cooling"); eff["holding_effects"]["mechanical_clear"] = True` changed `validate_lifecycle_landing("cooling")` from `True` to `False` and made subsequent `lifecycle_effects("cooling")` report `mechanical_clear=True`.
  - `engine/us_short_theme_lifecycle.py::next_theme_lifecycle_state` exposes `upgrade_confirm_runs` without validating the up-slow invariant. Codex probe: `upgrade_confirm_runs=0` or `1` returned `("confirmed_active", 0)` after one confirming run, while the design / preset require consecutive confirmation before upgrade.
  - `tests/test_us_short_theme_lifecycle.py` has positive coverage for the default two-run upgrade and a planted direct mutation of `TRANSITION_ACTIONS`, but it does not prove that the public `lifecycle_effects()` API is copy/immutable-safe, and it does not reject invalid one-run / zero-run upgrade thresholds.
- Why this is material: §4.3 / §18.0 make the lifecycle state machine a P0 downstream primitive for §4.2 scoring, §8 sizing, and §9 action ranking. The per-state effect table is claimed as frozen / single-sourced from the governance preset, and the validator is supposed to guarantee non-dangling plus no mechanical holding clear. Returning live mutable references lets ordinary downstream row-building code accidentally corrupt that contract process-wide. Allowing a caller-provided `upgrade_confirm_runs <= 1` weakens the required anti-chatter rule from up-slow consecutive confirmation to immediate upgrade.
- Required repair:
  1. Make lifecycle effects safe for consumers: do not expose mutable live references from the frozen transition-action table through `lifecycle_effects()` (return a deep copy or immutable recursive mapping), and avoid leaving a public mutable table as the normal consumer path. Add an adversarial test proving that mutating the returned effect cannot change later `lifecycle_effects()` / `validate_lifecycle_landing()` results.
  2. Enforce the up-slow anti-chatter invariant at the API boundary: invalid `upgrade_confirm_runs` values that do not require consecutive confirmation (0 / 1, and any same-class bad values) must fail closed or be ignored in favor of the frozen prior. Add reverse tests for 0 / 1 plus positive controls for the default two-run upgrade, deterioration precedence, stable reset, and retired re-entry gate.
  3. Keep overextension behavior intact unless a repair touches shared helpers; do not broaden into core_score, sizing, action_rank, batch3 validators/renderers, provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker work.
- Evidence collected by Codex: target tests passed (`python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_theme_lifecycle tests.test_us_short_overextension`: 28 OK); US-short discover passed (`tests -p '*us_short*'`: 583 OK); US-short schema passed (408 OK); doc-governance/route guards passed (38 OK); `git diff --check` returned 0 with CRLF warnings only. Independent probes reproduced the mutable returned-effect corruption and the 0/1 confirmation bypass. Overextension probes confirmed single-condition / K-1 / warning / missing-ATR cases did not produce `chasing_extreme`.
- Closure requires Claude `fix` to address the lifecycle API mutability and invalid upgrade-threshold guard class with tests, then Codex re-`review` to confirm the probes fail before / pass after, target US-short suites remain green, route/log docs are accurate, and no gated provider/live/DataHub/A-share/production work was added.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged both findings valid + accepted (in-scope, material — API-boundary safety class: a "frozen" table leaked a live mutable reference, and an anti-chatter invariant was caller-overridable). Fixed narrowly in `engine/us_short_theme_lifecycle.py` + its tests; overextension untouched. **(1) immutable effects**: `lifecycle_effects()` now returns `copy.deepcopy(TRANSITION_ACTIONS[state])`, so a consumer mutating the returned dict cannot corrupt the single-source governance table process-wide — Codex's `eff["holding_effects"]["mechanical_clear"]=True` probe is now harmless and later `lifecycle_effects()` / `validate_lifecycle_landing()` are unaffected. **(2) up-slow invariant at the API boundary**: `next_theme_lifecycle_state()` now fail-closes (raises ValueError) on an `upgrade_confirm_runs` that is non-int / bool / < 2, so 0 or 1 can no longer weaken consecutive-confirmation into an immediate upgrade; a stricter forward value (e.g. 3) is still allowed. **Tests**: added `test_returned_effect_is_copy_safe` (mutating the returned effect leaves later calls + validator unchanged), `test_upgrade_confirm_runs_below_two_fails_closed` (0 / 1 / -1 / bool / float / None → ValueError), and `test_stricter_three_run_upgrade_is_allowed` (3-run positive control); the existing default-2 upgrade / deterioration-precedence / stable-reset / retired-re-entry-gate positive controls remain. README is left unchanged — its "LOADED from the frozen governance table (single source)" claim stays accurate (now also immutable-safe), so no doc-content drift. Verify: lifecycle+overextension 31 OK (+3); tests/ us_short 586 OK + tests/schema 408 OK (zero regression); independent probe confirms the returned-effect mutation is harmless and 0/1 thresholds raise; BOM=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; doc-governance/route 38 OK. No provider/live/DataHub/A-share/core_score/sizing/action_rank/batch3/broker path. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-HARDVETO-RELIABLE-TRIGGER-ROW-CONTEXT-GAP - US-short batch2 hard-veto classifier misses a design-required reliable liquidity/spread hard trigger and silently downgrades bad row context

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was open P1 (2026-06-21 Codex review FAIL).
- Severity: **P1**.
- Scope reviewed: current dirty working tree US-short batch2 second slice (`engine/us_short_regime.py`, `engine/us_short_hard_veto.py`, `tests/test_us_short_regime.py`, `tests/test_us_short_hard_veto.py`, plus route/log docs). No provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_hard_veto.py::_RELIABLE_HARD` omits the US-short design's reliable hard-risk category for severe liquidity/spread risk. The authority says bottom-line / reliable file-status-price-class risks include `流动性枯竭` / `严重流动性/spread`; current classifier returns `veto_tier="none"` for plausible structured inputs such as `severe_liquidity`, `liquidity_dried`, `wide_spread`, `severe_spread`, `critical_spread`, and `illiquid`.
  - `engine/us_short_hard_veto.py::classify_hard_veto` chooses `position_hard_veto` only when `row_context == "holding"` and otherwise silently falls back to `entry_hard_veto`. Invalid or row-source-like values such as `position`, `holding_in_top15`, empty string, or `None` therefore convert a holding hard-risk into an entry-only effect instead of failing closed or mapping explicitly.
  - `tests/test_us_short_hard_veto.py::test_each_reliable_signal_hard_vetoes_candidate` loops over `hv._RELIABLE_HARD` itself, so it cannot catch a design-required trigger missing from `_RELIABLE_HARD`. `test_must_not_solo_count_matches_preset` similarly guards only the count of solo signals, not exact design-member mapping.
- Why this is material: §5 hard veto is a downstream safety primitive for §8 sizing / §9 action ranking. If liquidity/spread collapse is not classified as a reliable hard-risk, a bottom-line reject can pass as no veto. If a holding context is misspelled or passed as a row-source value, the classifier can label a holding hard-risk as entry-only, weakening the required holding re-evaluation / reduce / exit path.
- Required repair:
  1. Add explicit severe liquidity/spread reliable trigger(s) to the hard-veto classifier with stable structured input key(s) and reason labels, mapping candidates to `entry_hard_veto` and holdings to `position_hard_veto`.
  2. Add golden expected reliable-trigger set tests that are anchored to the design-required category set rather than only looping over `_RELIABLE_HARD`; include the liquidity/spread trigger and at least one positive control per row context.
  3. Validate `row_context` strictly (`candidate` / `holding`) or provide an explicit row-source-to-context mapper. Invalid, missing, or misspelled contexts must not silently fall back to candidate behavior. Add reverse tests for bad contexts.
  4. Strengthen the must-not-solo guard from count-only to exact member mapping if the test continues to claim complete §5.3 solo-signal coverage.
  5. Update `docs/README.md` / `docs/SESSION_LOG.md` wording if it continues to enumerate §5.1a reliable hard triggers or complete §5.3 coverage without these guards.
  6. Keep the repair narrow: no provider/live/network/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production/broker path and no unrelated batch2 slice.
- Evidence collected by Codex: `python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_regime tests.test_us_short_hard_veto` passed 30 tests; `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*us_short*'` passed 547 tests. Independent probes showed all tested liquidity/spread keys returned `veto_tier="none"` and invalid contexts (`position`, `holding_in_top15`, empty string, `None`) silently returned `entry_hard_veto` for a reliable hard trigger.
- Closure requires Codex re-`审查` to confirm the reliable-trigger category set includes the design-required liquidity/spread hard risk, row context handling is fail-closed or explicitly mapped, same-class tests fail before / pass after the fix, target US-short suites remain green, and no gated provider/live/DataHub/A-share/production work was added.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged all 3 findings valid + accepted (in-scope, material — same whole-class/validity-gate class as the price-engine slice: an incomplete §5.1a category set + a silent context fallback + self-referential tests). Fixed narrowly in `engine/us_short_hard_veto.py` + its tests, nothing else. **(1) liquidity/spread reliable trigger**: added `severe_liquidity` (流动性枯竭) + `severe_spread` (严重spread) to `_RELIABLE_HARD` — the design §5.1a 严重流动性/spread category — mapping candidate→entry_hard_veto, holding→position_hard_veto (the stable contract keys `severe_liquidity` / `severe_spread` return hard veto; broader alias names such as `wide_spread` are not contract keys and are not claimed). **(2) row_context fail-closed**: `classify_hard_veto` now raises `ValueError` for any context other than `candidate` / `holding`, so `position` / `holding_in_top15` / `''` / `None` / typos no longer silently become entry_hard_veto; added `row_source_to_context()` mapping the 4 frozen action_table `row_source` values (holding_*→holding, top15_candidate→candidate; unknown raises). **(3) golden / exact tests**: added `ReliableHardVetoGoldenTests` anchored to a hardcoded design-required set (incl. liquidity/spread) — NOT a loop over `_RELIABLE_HARD`, so a missing required trigger fails — with a positive control per row context; `RowContextValidationTests` (bad contexts raise; mapper covers exactly the frozen `row_source` enum); and `test_must_not_solo_exact_member_mapping` upgrading §5.3 from count-only to exact preset-item↔engine-key mapping. README §5.1a enumeration updated (+ liquidity/spread, + row_context strictness, + golden / exact-mapping guards); the historical 起草 SESSION_LOG entry is left as the original draft record (this 修复 entry is the live correction). Verify: hard-veto+regime target 38 OK (+8); tests/ us_short 555 OK + tests/schema 408 OK (zero regression); independent probe confirms severe_liquidity/spread → hard veto and all 4 bad contexts raise fail-closed; BOM=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; doc-governance/route 38 OK. No provider/live/DataHub/A-share/sizing/broker path.

### R-USSHORT-BATCH2-PRICE-STRUCTURE-FAILURE-RESCUE-GAP - US-short batch2 price engine can convert invalid structures into executable or false breach signals

- Status: **resolved** (committed in the 2026-06-21 US-short batch-2 build, Codex re-`审查 PASS`). Was OPEN P1 (2026-06-21 Codex review FAIL).
- Scope reviewed: current `master@f646147f` working tree US-short batch2 first slice (`engine/us_short_price_engine.py`, `engine/us_short_private_paths.py`, related tests and route/log docs). No provider/live/DataHub/A-share/Skill/production path was executed.
- Technical finding:
  - `engine/us_short_price_engine.py::holding_exit_engine` treats post-round take-profit structure failure as an actual stop breach. With `close=109.0`, `support=95.0`, `resistance=109.001`, `atr=2.0`, the rounded TP levels become invalid while price is still above `stop_clear_price=106.51`; the function returns `executable=True`, `reject_reason="取整后止盈结构失效(已破位)"`, and `trace.breached=True`. This fabricates a breach signal for a non-breached holding.
  - `engine/us_short_price_engine.py::support_atr_engine` silently rescues an invalid pullback entry band. With `close=100.0`, `effective_support=101.0`, `effective_resistance=110.0`, `atr=2.0`, the raw pullback band is contradictory (`valid_low_raw > valid_high_raw`), but the code collapses the band to `(100.0, 100.0)` and returns an executable plan instead of degrading/observing.
- Why this is material: §6/§6.1 make the price engine a downstream decision primitive. Future action tables, holding decisions, and private reports can consume `executable`, `breached`, stop/TP fields, and reject reasons directly. Passing unit tests are not enough if invalid geometry is silently converted into usable signals.
- Required repair:
  1. Split actual stop breach from post-round TP structure failure in `holding_exit_engine`. If `close > stop_clear_price`, do not set `trace.breached=True` and do not use an `已破位` reason solely because TP levels rounded into an invalid order. Choose an explicit design-compatible fallback (stop-only/risk-only/observe), but keep the breach flag honest.
  2. Do not rescue contradictory support-entry bands into a current-price executable plan. If pullback raw/tick-rounded band is structurally invalid (for example support above close after validation), degrade/fail closed with an explicit non-executable reason unless there is a separately justified design case.
  3. Add same-class tests covering non-breached TP-round failure, true stop breach positive control, contradictory pullback band rejection, and a valid pullback band control.
- Evidence collected by Codex: `python -m unittest tests.test_us_short_price_engine tests.test_us_short_private_paths` passed 36 tests; `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*us_short*'` passed 515 tests; `python -m unittest tests.test_doc_governance_guard tests.test_route_doc_ledger_status_consistency` passed 38 tests. Independent probes reproduced both failure modes above.
- Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权): judged both findings valid + accepted (in-scope, material — same draft-validity-gates class my pre-Codex self-review `C` missed: the "valid geometry" precondition set was not enumerated adversarially). Fixed exactly the 2 silent-rescue / false-signal paths in `engine/us_short_price_engine.py`, nothing else touched. **(1) holding breach vs TP-failure split**: `holding_exit_engine` keeps the true breach branch (`close ≤ stop_clear_price` → `breached=True`, unchanged), but a post-round take-profit structure failure when `close > stop` is NO LONGER treated as a breach — it now emits the valid `stop_clear_price`, sets `take_profit_reduce_price`/`take_profit_exit_price = None`, `post_round_rr_status="tp_not_computable"`, `breached=False`, reason "止盈位取整后不可精算(止损有效,未破位)". So Codex's `close=109 / resistance=109.001 / atr=2` case returns `breached=False`, stop `106.51` present, TP `None` (no fabricated 已破位). **(2) pullback invalid-structure fail-closed**: added an explicit `support ≥ close → observe` precondition (a pullback support must be BELOW price) AND removed the silent band-collapse rescue — a contradictory/degenerate `valid_low_t > valid_high_t` band now returns observe ("入场区间取整后失效…") instead of collapsing to the current price and shipping an executable plan (the band check sits after the sub_mode branch, so it also fail-closes a degenerate breakout band). Independent probe: the design line containing `cash_allocation_rank` contains `可建仓票`, while schema properties/required are only `schema_name`, `schema_version`, `as_of`, `status`, `cash_allocation_fields`, `ordering_keys`, `conservative_entry_basis`, `sequential_allocation`, `insufficient_cash_to_observe`, `ordering_weight_calibration_item_id`, and `notes`; tokens `allocation_scope`, `only_buildable`, `never_rescue`, `non_buildable`, and `cash_allocation_input_scope` are absent from schema/preset/tests. The word "buildable" appears only in schema descriptions, not as a schema-enforced contract.

Materiality: this is not a current runtime regression because the slice is declarative and no batch-2 cash allocator consumes it yet. It is material before implementation because cash allocation is a downstream sizing gate, not a rescue or admission gate. If a future consumer trusts the current schema, it can allocate or rank all candidates, including observe / veto / non-buildable rows, while still satisfying the governance contract. That can let a downstream implementation use cash ordering to revive rows that earlier gates made non-buildable, or waste allocation state on rows that should never enter the cash allocation queue. The project has repeatedly treated these under-pinned schema contracts as P1 before executable consumers are written.

Required repair: make the buildable-only scope schema-enforced instead of relying on prose. Acceptable repair shape: add structured const-pinned preset/schema fields such as `allocation_input_scope = "buildable_tickers_only"` plus `never_rescue_non_buildable = true`, or an equivalent object that proves cash allocation consumes only rows already eligible for new build and cannot turn observe / veto / hard-veto / cooldown / portfolio-guard-blocked rows back into build candidates. Add negative schema tests rejecting `all_candidates`, rejecting `observe_or_veto_allowed`, rejecting `never_rescue_non_buildable=false`, and proving provenance covers §8 `可建仓票` in addition to `valid_entry_high` / cash floor phrases. Update the README route row and handoff wording if needed so they teach the buildable-only scope. Keep ordering-weight values routed to §13.1 #25; do not implement batch-2 engine logic or pin actual weight numbers.

Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short §8 symbol-cooldown governance slice, including `schemas/us_short_symbol_cooldown_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_symbol_cooldown_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_symbol_cooldown_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `docs/system_risk_register.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §8 / §18.1 #16 / §13.1 #23, the action-table contract, and the lifecycle calibration registry.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-SYMBOL-COOLDOWN-FILLED-BREAKOUT-PRECONDITION-GAP`): the governance slice correctly pins the broad no-penalty-if-unfilled rule and the anti-revenge-buy re-entry AND gate, but it does not structure the design's stricter fill precondition for breakout failure cooldown entry. The live design authority says both: §8 "突破单未成交 = 不进冷静期（没进场不罚）" and §18.1 #16 "突破单未成交不进冷静期、成交后失败才进 `symbol_cooldown`". The schema/preset/tests instead pin `enters_cooldown_on = ["filled_then_stop_loss", "breakout_failure"]`. There is no const-pinned `filled_then_breakout_failure`, no `breakout_failure_requires_fill` / `requires_fill` field, and the provenance test checks "突破失败" but not the stricter "成交后失败才进" mechanic. Independent probe: the design line containing `symbol_cooldown` includes "成交后失败才进", while schema/preset/test all contain broad `breakout_failure` and contain none of `filled_then_breakout_failure`, `breakout_failure_requires_fill`, or `requires_fill`.

Materiality: this is not a current runtime regression because the slice is declarative and no engine consumes it yet. It is material before batch-2 implementation because a future cooldown engine can read the schema-valid trigger `breakout_failure` as "breakout order did not fill / breakout setup failed" and enter cooldown despite the design explicitly saying unfilled breakout orders must not be penalized. That weakens the safety contract in both directions: it can falsely block valid future entries, and it hides the exact event boundary the tests are supposed to preserve before executable price/cooldown logic is written.

Required repair: make the filled precondition schema-enforced instead of relying on prose. Acceptable repair shapes include either replacing the trigger token with `filled_then_breakout_failure`, or restructuring triggers as objects that const-pin `event=breakout_failure` plus `requires_fill=true`, while preserving `filled_then_stop_loss` and `breakout_unfilled_no_cooldown=true`. Add negative schema tests rejecting a broad / unqualified `breakout_failure`, rejecting `requires_fill=false` or missing for breakout failure, and proving the provenance test covers §18.1 #16 "成交后失败才进 `symbol_cooldown`" in addition to §8. Update the README route row and current handoff wording so they do not teach "breakout-failure" without the filled precondition. Keep `param_calibration_item_id=23` routed to lifecycle; do not pin cooldown length or recovery thresholds.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-21, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid + accepted — §18.1 #16 "成交后失败才进 `symbol_cooldown`" disambiguates §8's "成交后触发止损 / 突破失败" so the fill precondition applies to breakout-failure cooldown entry too; my broad `breakout_failure` token dropped it and was internally inconsistent with my own `breakout_unfilled_no_cooldown=true`. Chose repair shape (a): replaced the token with `filled_then_breakout_failure` so `enters_cooldown_on = ["filled_then_stop_loss", "filled_then_breakout_failure"]` — both triggers now share the `filled_then_` prefix, making the fill precondition structural. Added `test_all_cooldown_triggers_require_fill` (every trigger must start with `filled_then_`), `test_schema_rejects_unqualified_breakout_failure` (broad `breakout_failure` rejected by const), and extended the provenance test to require §18.1 #16 "成交后失败才进" + "突破单未成交不进冷静期" (not just §8 "突破失败"). Updated the schema/preset descriptions + a preset note (`cooldown_entry_requires_fill`) + the README trigger wording so none teach unqualified breakout-failure. Kept `filled_then_stop_loss`, `breakout_unfilled_no_cooldown=true`, `param_calibration_item_id=23`; pinned no cooldown length/recovery thresholds. Ripple (surfaced while landing this fix, process-infra not business): the doc-governance review-cycle guard's block-split only recognized the em-dash header separator, so this em-dash `修复` entry absorbed the following hyphen-headed Codex `review FAIL` entry (Codex's newer "- Codex `review …`" format) → false duplicate-label + free-form offenders; an independent both-separator probe showed the only other affected entry was a 2026-06-17 Codex entry whose archive-note blockquote read as free-form. Hardened the guard (single-source `_review_cycle_offenders` + `_draft_handoff_proof_offenders`): split now accepts `—`/`–`/`-` separators, and the bullet-line check skips `>` blockquote lines; added two positive-control planted assertions (a hyphen review header must isolate, a blockquote line must be skipped) so a split regression re-fails. RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-21): US-short two-axis regime governance schema under-pins §7 input-axis and safety mechanics. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-REGIME-GOVERNANCE-INPUT-AXES-UNDERPINNED`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future batch-2 regime+sizing consumer / provider-gate safety before any engine consumes the governance artifact). Scope reviewed: current dirty US-short §7 regime governance slice, including `schemas/us_short_regime_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_regime_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_regime_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `docs/system_risk_register.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §7/§8/§13.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-REGIME-GOVERNANCE-INPUT-AXES-UNDERPINNED`): the preset and tests pin the four `market_risk_regime` caps, the high-level two-axis booleans, anti-chatter booleans, `unknown_defaults_defensive`, scope booleans, and `threshold_calibration_item_id=3`, but several design-locked §7 mechanics are still only prose in `description`/`notes` or absent from the schema/preset. Specifically, the schema has no const-pinned field for the risk-axis input set `VIX + SPY/QQQ + breadth`; no machine field proving QQQ is required in the market-trend axis; no field for `VIX 未授权 / unavailable` becoming an unknown axis with fallback to `SPY/QQQ + breadth` plus conservative unknown downgrade; no field that breadth comes from the base universe and does not depend on paid industry ETFs; no structured unknown-severity policy for `缺一项降级 / 缺关键项至少防御 / 严重 restricted`; and no const for the explicit upgrade confirmation rule `连续 2 次周跑更好或站回阈值上方缓冲`. Independent probe: the design §7 contains all of `必须含 QQQ`, `VIX 未授权 / unavailable`, `缺一项降级`, and `连续 2 次周跑`; the schema properties `risk_axis_inputs`, `vix_unavailable_policy`, `unknown_degradation_policy`, and `upgrade_confirmation_weekly_runs` are all absent; the preset does not mention `QQQ`, base-universe breadth, or `unapproved`. Existing tests pass because they only assert the current cap ladder and coarse booleans, not schema rejection for these same-class contract drifts.

Materiality: this is the same schema-contract class as the earlier US-short under-pinning findings: the current artifact is meant to freeze §7 before the batch-2 regime/position engine consumes it. If a future consumer trusts this schema, it can validate a governance artifact or implementation path that drops QQQ, uses only SPY, treats VIX provider-unavailable as clean/aggressive, depends on paid industry ETFs for breadth, upgrades after one good week, or weakens missing-input downgrades. That can change the market-risk cap and new-entry permission while still appearing schema-valid. The current slice has no executable engine yet, so this is not a runtime regression, but it is material before engine/provider/DataHub work.

Required repair: make the §7 governance schema reject the missing mechanics instead of leaving them as prose. Acceptable repair shape: add structured const-pinned preset/schema fields for (1) `risk_axis_inputs` or equivalent with VIX, SPY+QQQ trend, and breadth as the full `worst_of` component set; (2) QQQ-required and breadth-source/no-paid-industry-ETF policy; (3) VIX provider authorization/unavailable policy (`unapproved/unavailable` -> axis `unknown`, fallback to SPY/QQQ+breadth, conservative unknown downgrade); (4) unknown severity rules (`missing_one_downgrade`, `missing_critical_at_least_defensive`, `severe_restricted` or exact equivalents); and (5) upgrade confirmation (`downgrade_immediate`, `upgrade_confirmation_weekly_runs=2`, threshold-buffer alternative). Add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` for dropping QQQ, dropping breadth, changing VIX-unavailable to aggressive/clean, requiring paid industry ETF breadth, weakening unknown downgrade, and reducing upgrade confirmation to one week. Keep threshold numeric values such as VIX 18/25/35 routed to §13.1 #3, and keep §8 `theme_probe` sizing/count details out of this repair unless the repair intentionally touches the §8 portfolio-guard slice. Boundary: regime governance schema/preset/tests, README route wording, minimal SESSION_LOG closeout, and this register only; do not implement batch-2 engine logic, provider calls, DataHub, runner consumption, market fetch, broker/order automation, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Independent adversarial probe: a `Claude (US-short 批X 起草)` handoff with `**Worked on**: discussed Proof-of-use wording...`, no `**Pre-Codex self-review**:` / `**Proof-of-use**:` line, and `**Next**: Codex 审查` returned `[]`. Closure still requires..." after the round-2 resolution, so the Hot Queue now simultaneously says resolved and still-open for the same prior issue.

Materiality: the project rule requires an explicit proof line because future reviewers need a mechanically visible A-F self-review record, not just incidental prose containing a keyword. A substring check lets exactly the same "proof not actually left" class recur under wording that mentions the rule. The stale register paragraph is also cross-LLM continuity risk: a fresh agent can read the same Hot Queue item as both resolved and unresolved.

Required repair: make `_draft_handoff_proof_offenders` require an actual proof label/line, not a substring anywhere in the block. Acceptable shape: reuse the existing bullet/label parser or a line-level regex that only accepts `**Pre-Codex self-review**:` / `**Proof-of-use**:` (with optional list marker), then add a planted failure where prose mentions `Proof-of-use` but no proof label exists. Keep the current false-positive controls for non-draft `执行`, Codex review entries, and real proof-line entries. Also rewrite or remove the stale prior "still FAIL / open" paragraph so the register has one current state. Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 weekly_report output contract, including `schemas/us_short_weekly_report_contract.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_weekly_report_contract_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_weekly_report_contract_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §11.2 / §11.3 / §18.1 #9/#11/#12. **Resolution**: judged valid + accepted (my schema/test split — schema shape-only + test guards Chinese content — left 3 same-shape-drift holes the schema itself accepted; the "avoid hardcoding Chinese" rationale was over-cautious since the Write tool handles UTF-8 and a triangulation test catches transcription; this is the same lesson as `R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-GOVERNANCE-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED` — a contract schema must const-pin governed identity, not just test it). **Whole-class fix** (audited every property, not just the 3 named): (1) `sections` now const-pinned in the schema (exact 13 Chinese strings, byte-copied from the design-generated preset) + a triangulation test asserts schema const == preset == design §11.2 extraction; (2) `mandatory_banner.elements[].tag` const-pinned per element (5); (3) `lifecycle_reminder_count_consistency` restructured from a free prose string to a const object {rule, section_number_a=1, section_number_b=12, must_match=true}. Audited the rest: `status`/banner `ref`/`notes` stay typed because they are legitimately variable/descriptive, NOT governed identity (consistent with the PASS'd action_table contract). Added negative schema tests for all 3 holes (section rename + reorder, banner tag drift, lifecycle weaken + section-number drift) — independent probe confirms each is now rejected. Verify: weekly_report tests 19→24 OK; full discover 2940 OK (zero regression, +5 net); BOM=0; diff-check CLEAN. No provider/render/fetch path.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-WEEKLY-REPORT-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`): the preset and tests currently match the design, but the schema does not actually freeze several governed constants that the slice claims to freeze. `sections` is only `minItems=maxItems=13` with string items, so a 13-item array with arbitrary or reordered section titles validates. `lifecycle_reminder_count_consistency` is only a non-empty string, so the "section 1 == section 12" invariant can be replaced by arbitrary text and still validates. `mandatory_banner.elements[*].tag` is only a non-empty string, so the machine-readable banner identities can drift while ids/count/always_shown still pass. Independent schema mutation probe results: `rename_section_same_count=ACCEPTED`, `reorder_sections_same_count=ACCEPTED`, `lifecycle_rule_drift=ACCEPTED`, and `banner_tag_drift=ACCEPTED`. Existing tests catch the committed preset's design faithfulness, but they do not require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for those same-count / same-shape schema drifts.

Materiality: this file is a batch-1 declarative output contract meant to freeze the §11.2 weekly_report surface before the batch-3 renderer and field_registry consumers exist. If a future renderer or registry gate trusts schema validation, it can accept a contract where "Top15 选股" or "字段·模块生命周期提醒" has been renamed/reordered, where lifecycle count consistency is no longer section 1 vs section 12, or where the price-clock banner id points to a different tag. That weakens the same no-dangling / honest-output guarantee this slice is supposed to establish, even though the current preset happens to be correct.

Required repair: make the schema reject governed weekly_report identity drift, not just the current preset tests. At minimum const-pin the full ordered 13-section array in `sections` (it is acceptable to generate that const mechanically from `docs/us_short_system_design.md`, but the tracked schema must validate the exact set/order), const-pin or structurally encode `lifecycle_reminder_count_consistency` so the rule cannot drift away from section 1 == section 12, and const-pin the five banner `tag` machine ids (`true_false_observe_split`, `macro_cluster_warning`, `ship_gate_progress`, `price_clock`, `hot_excluded_notice`) in their current order. Add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` for same-count section rename, same-count section reorder, lifecycle rule drift, and banner tag drift. Keep the design single-source test so schema consts stay byte-faithful to §11.2, and update README/SESSION_LOG wording if the schema-vs-test split changes. Boundary: weekly_report schema / preset / schema tests / README route row / this register only; do not implement renderer, field_registry, row-level no-dangling validator, batch-2 engine, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short action_table output contract omits design-locked vocabularies for `theme_source` and `macro_cluster_warning_level`. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACTION-TABLE-DESIGN-LOCKED-VOCAB-GAP`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future action_table producer, no-dangling validator, renderer, and field_registry consumer integrity before batch 2/3 consumers exist). Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 action_table output contract, including `schemas/us_short_action_table_contract.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_action_table_contract_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_action_table_contract_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 / §8 / §10 / §11.3 / §11.5 / §18.1 #9/#15. **Resolution**: judged valid + accepted (independently re-read design — `theme_source`（§4.3 l148: `gics_established` / `provisional_discovered`）and `macro_cluster_warning_level`（§8 l228: `none / elevated / high`, only frac thresholds = §13 #31 forward, labels locked — structurally identical to the already-pinned `portfolio_guard_status`）both ARE design-locked). Root cause = my §A whole-class sweep covered only the `∈ {…}` convention and missed the equivalent `` `field`（v / v）`` convention. **Whole-class fix (not just the 2 named)**: (1) const-pinned both in schema (required enum keys 12→14) + preset + `EXPECTED_ENUMS`; (2) **exhaustively re-swept all 16 remaining deferred columns under BOTH conventions** → confirmed NO third column carries a value vocab (the rest are field-name lists / numerics / free tags / prose); (3) added a recurrence guard `test_set_notation_vocabs_fully_covered` (auto-discovers every `field ∈ {…}` column-vocab in the design and asserts it is pinned + exact — planted-failure-verified) + `test_parenthetical_vocab_values_are_in_design` (single-source check on the two parenthetical vocabs) + 3 negative schema tests (theme_source/macro_cluster_warning_level drift + dropped-required-enum). Verify: action_table tests 21→26 OK; full discover 2916 OK (zero regression, +5 net); BOM=0; diff-check CLEAN. No provider/engine/fetch path.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACTION-TABLE-DESIGN-LOCKED-VOCAB-GAP`): the contract says it const-pins the §11.3 column set and all design-locked action_table vocabularies, but two action_table columns with explicit design vocabularies are left outside `design_locked_enums` and are even listed in `notes.deferred_vocab_columns`. `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 says `theme_source` values are `gics_established / provisional_discovered`; §8 says `macro_cluster_warning_level` values are `none / elevated / high`; §11.3 includes both columns in `action_table.csv`. Independent probe confirms both are core columns (`in_columns=True`) and both are not enum-pinned (`enum_pinned=False`). Existing tests still pass because `EXPECTED_ENUMS` hard-codes the incomplete 12-key set and does not assert these two design vocabularies.

Materiality: `theme_source` drives established-vs-provisional theme provenance and interacts with lifecycle / provisional-theme reporting, while `macro_cluster_warning_level=high` is designed to affect `risk_tags`, `action_confidence`, `model_position_size`, and the weekly report cluster banner. If future batch-2 row production or batch-3 validation trusts this contract, arbitrary values for these two columns can pass the shared contract while downstream aggregation / no-dangling / rendering logic assumes canonical tokens. That is the same contract-trust class this slice is meant to prevent before any consumer exists.

Required repair: add `theme_source` and `macro_cluster_warning_level` to `design_locked_enums` in schema and preset, const-pinned respectively to `["gics_established", "provisional_discovered"]` and `["none", "elevated", "high"]`. Remove both from the deferred-vocab note, update README/SESSION_LOG wording if needed, and add negative schema tests requiring `jsonschema.ValidationError` when either vocabulary drifts or is omitted. Keep positive cross-checks that these keys are real core columns. Boundary: action_table schema / preset / schema tests / README route row / this register only; do not implement row-level validator, batch-2 engine, batch-3 renderer/no-dangling, field_registry, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short theme-lifecycle governance omits the design-required `cooling` holding decay tag / §9 re-evaluation path. status `resolved`(working tree; Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-20; pending 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-THEME-LIFECYCLE-COOLING-HOLDING-EFFECT-GAP`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future lifecycle classifier and report validator before batch 2/3 consumers exist). Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 theme-lifecycle governance, including `schemas/us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_theme_lifecycle_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.3 / §10 / §11.3 / §13.1 #30 / §18.1 #14.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-THEME-LIFECYCLE-COOLING-HOLDING-EFFECT-GAP`): the design requires every degraded lifecycle state (`cooling`, `decayed`, and `retired`) to add a `theme_decay` tag to holdings and trigger §9 re-evaluation, while not mechanically clearing the holding. It also separately says `cooling` lowers holding `action_confidence`. The current governed action table const-pins `cooling.holding_effect = "action_confidence_down"` only; `decayed` and `retired` are the only states with `"theme_decay_tag_and_reeval"`. Independent probe confirms the schema-valid preset has `cooling` holding effect with no `theme_decay` and no `reeval`, while `decayed` / `retired` contain both. The tests do not catch the gap: `test_no_state_mechanically_clears_a_holding` comments "cooling/decayed/retired tag + re-evaluate" but only asserts `mechanical_clear == false`, and no test requires `cooling` to carry the tag / re-eval effect.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §18.1 #14 says `theme_lifecycle_state` must affect seats / position / confidence / risk tags / observe reason and includes "持仓加 `theme_decay` 标 + §9 重评、不机械清仓". If a future lifecycle classifier or report validator trusts this governance artifact, a `cooling` theme can lower confidence without marking held names for the required decay review path. That weakens the no-dangling contract around `theme_lifecycle_state` and can let degraded themes avoid the review surface that the design explicitly requires before any batch 2/3 consumer exists.

Required repair: encode the full holding effect for `cooling`, not only the confidence effect. Acceptable repair shapes include splitting `holding_effect` into structured booleans / arrays (for example confidence_down + theme_decay_tag + section9_reeval + mechanical_clear=false) or const-pinning an unambiguous combined value for `cooling` that preserves both `action_confidence_down` and `theme_decay_tag_and_reeval`. Add tests that assert `cooling`, `decayed`, and `retired` all carry the theme-decay tag + §9 re-evaluation path, and that `cooling` still lowers confidence. Add negative schema tests requiring rejection when `cooling` loses either side of the combined holding effect. Update README wording if the field shape changes. Boundary: theme-lifecycle schema / preset / schema tests / README route row / this register only; do not implement the batch-2 lifecycle classifier, batch-3 validator/reporting, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — my single `holding_effect` enum collapsed the multi-dimensional holding effects, so `cooling` (which the design needs to BOTH lower action_confidence AND, like decayed/retired, add the theme_decay tag + trigger §9 re-eval) only carried `action_confidence_down`, dropping the design-required decay-review path (§18.1 #14 + §4.3 「cooling/decayed/retired 持仓加 theme_decay 标 + §9 重评、不机械清仓」). Same multi-member-coverage failure the just-strengthened checklist §A targets, here on the effect-DIMENSIONS × states matrix. Repair: replaced the `holding_effect` enum + top-level `mechanical_clear` with a structured `holding_effects` object const-pinned per state {action_confidence_down, theme_decay_tag, section9_reeval, mechanical_clear}. Now cooling = {confidence true, decay_tag true, reeval true, clear false}; decayed/retired = {confidence false, decay_tag true, reeval true, clear false}; provisional/confirmed = all false. Tests: `test_degraded_states_carry_theme_decay_tag_and_section9_reeval` (cooling/decayed/retired all tag+reeval; active none) + `test_only_cooling_lowers_confidence`; negative schema tests `test_schema_rejects_cooling_loses_theme_decay_tag` / `_section9_reeval` / `_confidence_down` (cooling losing either side of the combined effect is rejected) + the mechanical_clear mutation path updated; updated README to the structured shape. Verify: theme-lifecycle schema tests 21 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2890 OK (zero regression; +5 net); cooling holding_effects = confidence+decay_tag+reeval (no mechanical_clear), the cooling-drop mutations now rejected, real preset still validates; BOM/FFFD=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; no provider/broker/fetch. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short scoring-profile shadow comparison weights remain schema-accepting invalid drift. status `resolved`(working tree; Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-20; pending 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-SHADOW-WEIGHT-SCHEMA-GAP`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future shadow comparison evidence integrity before batch 3 comparison-track consumers exist). Scope reviewed: Codex re-review of Claude repair for `R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-GOVERNANCE-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`, including `schemas/us_short_scoring_profile_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_scoring_profile_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_scoring_profile_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.2 / §12.2 / §13.1 #28 / §18.1 #13.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-SHADOW-WEIGHT-SCHEMA-GAP`): the prior four mutation cases are fixed, but `theme_plus` and `theme_aggressive` still use the generic `weightsShape` schema. Schema validation therefore accepts invalid shadow comparison weights. Independent probes: `theme_plus.weights={momentum:0.9, theme:0.9, catalyst:0.9}` validates successfully even though weights sum to 2.7; `theme_aggressive.weights={momentum:0.8, theme:0.1, catalyst:0.1}` validates successfully even though the profile is no longer an aggressive theme-overweight comparison档. The current tests catch the committed preset's sum-to-one and theme ordering, but they do not require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for these shadow-weight drift cases. This leaves the same schema-consumer trust gap that the previous Required was meant to close, only moved from `balanced` / `theme_off` to the two comparison profiles governed by §13.1 #28.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` makes `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` the shadow comparison tracks used to decide whether the main system is missing strong themes (§12.2), and §13.1 #28 explicitly routes comparison-profile weights and minimum comparison weeks through lifecycle calibration. Shadow tracks do not count toward ship-gate, but their future results can drive a reviewed promotion of the primary system. If a future comparison runner trusts schema validation and consumes non-normalized or non-theme-overweight weights, its evidence can be distorted while still appearing schema-valid.

Required repair: make the schema reject invalid `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` weight drift, not just the current preset tests. Preferred repair is to const-pin the current v1 prior weights (`theme_plus` 0.30/0.50/0.20; `theme_aggressive` 0.25/0.55/0.20) until a future reviewed §13 #28 calibration changes the schema/preset together, mirroring the local `egs_industry_heat_governance` precedent. If the implementer intentionally wants those two weights open, add an explicit structured rule (schema or a named validator consumed by future runners) that guarantees sum-to-one and preserves the intended ordering (`balanced.theme < theme_plus.theme < theme_aggressive.theme`, with nonnegative bounded weights) before any consumer can accept the artifact; document why exact const-pins are not used. Add negative tests requiring schema/validator rejection for at least `theme_plus` sum drift and `theme_aggressive` no-longer-aggressive drift. Boundary: schema / preset / scoring-profile tests / route-doc wording / this register only; do not implement batch 2 engine scoring, comparison-track runner, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — my prior repair const-pinned `balanced` + `theme_off` but left `theme_plus`/`theme_aggressive` on the generic shape (each 0-1, no sum/ordering), so a consumer could feed non-normalized or non-overweight shadow weights. Chose the PREFERRED repair (const-pin the v1 prior weights, mirroring `egs_industry_heat_governance` + my own balanced/theme_off pinning): split the shared `shadowComparisonProfile`/`weightsShape` into `themePlusProfile` (weights const {0.30,0.50,0.20}) + `themeAggressiveProfile` (weights const {0.25,0.55,0.20}), each keeping the role/live/shadow consts; removed the now-unused `weightsShape`. ALL four profiles' weights are now const-pinned at their v1 frozen values; a reviewed §13.1 #28 forward calibration changes the schema + preset together with a version bump (the prior status stays documented via `status` + each profile's `value_source` + the calibration routing). The governance tests still verify the frozen weights satisfy sum-to-one + the balanced<theme_plus<theme_aggressive ordering (sanity on the consts). Added negative schema tests `test_schema_rejects_theme_plus_weight_drift` ({0.9,0.9,0.9}, sum 2.7) + `test_schema_rejects_theme_aggressive_no_longer_aggressive` ({0.8,0.1,0.1}, theme underweight); updated schema description + README to say all weights are const-pinned. Verify: scoring-profile schema tests 17 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2869 OK (zero regression; +2 net); both shadow-weight mutations now rejected + real preset still validates; BOM/FFFD=0; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; no provider/broker/fetch. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 scoring-profile governance schema under-pins the governed constants. status `resolved`(working tree; Codex re-`审查 PASS` 2026-06-20; pending 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-GOVERNANCE-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`; severity `P1` (schema-contract / future scoring-profile consumer / shadow ship-gate isolation before batch 2+ engine and batch 3 comparison-track consumers exist). Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 scoring-profile governance, including `schemas/us_short_scoring_profile_governance.schema.json`, `presets/us_short_scoring_profile_governance_20260620.json`, `tests/schema/test_us_short_scoring_profile_governance_schema.py`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §4.2/§12.2/§13.1 #1/#28/§18.1 #13/#24.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-SCORING-PROFILE-GOVERNANCE-SCHEMA-UNDERPINNED`): the current preset values match the design, but the schema is only a generic profile-shape schema and does not reject critical drift in the governed constants. Independent schema-only mutation probe accepted all of these invalid documents: `theme_plus.live_eligible=true`, `balanced.weights.theme=0.99`, `theme_off.weights={momentum:1.0, theme:0.0, catalyst:0.0}` (not the proportional rollback baseline), and `min_comparison_weeks=1`. The test file validates the current preset and catches some current-artifact drift by direct assertions, but it does not assert `jsonschema.ValidationError` for those schema-contract mutations, and a future consumer that trusts schema validation would accept them. Local precedent for this exact class is `schemas/egs_industry_heat_governance.schema.json`, which const-pins every governed profile weight and has a negative schema test for profile weight drift.

Materiality: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` makes `scoring_profile` a named governance contract: `balanced` is the only primary / only `model_paper` main track, `theme_plus` / `theme_aggressive` / `theme_off` are shadow-only, shadow never counts toward ship-gate, and `theme_off` is the attribution / rollback baseline with theme weight zero redistributed to momentum + catalyst. If schema validation accepts a shadow profile flipped live, a primary weight drift, a non-proportional `theme_off`, or a one-week comparison threshold, batch 2/3 code can later consume an invalid but schema-valid governance artifact and weaken the §4.2 / §12.2 / §18.1 #13/#24 isolation. A related routing gap is that the artifact exposes only `calibration_item_id=28`; design §13.1 #1 governs the primary 40/35/25 weight prior, while #28 governs comparison-profile weights and minimum comparison weeks. Collapsing both into #28 can make lifecycle reminders miss or duplicate the primary-weight calibration path.

Required repair: make the schema and tests reject the invalid governance states, not merely document them. Acceptable repair shapes: const-pin each named profile's role, live/shadow flags, and weights in the schema (or equivalent draft-07 `if/then`/per-profile definitions), require the initial comparison horizon to be at least / exactly 12 weeks per the frozen prior, and encode the calibration routing explicitly (for example `primary_weight_calibration_item_id=1` plus `comparison_profile_calibration_item_id=28`, or an equivalent unambiguous structure). Add negative tests that mutate the preset and require `jsonschema.ValidationError` for at least: shadow profile flipped live, balanced weight drift, `theme_off` non-proportional / non-zero-theme drift, and comparison weeks below 12; keep the current positive preset validation. Boundary: schema / preset / scoring-profile tests / route-doc wording / this register only; do not implement batch 2 engine scoring, comparison-track runner, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted (both points) — my schema was generic shape-only with the governed constants enforced only in the test, but a consumer trusting schema validation would accept drift (the local `egs_industry_heat_governance` precedent const-pins weights in the schema; I knew it and did not follow it). **Repair 1 (schema under-pinned)**: replaced the single generic `profile` $def with three per-profile $defs that CONST-PIN the governed constants in the schema itself — `primaryProfile` (balanced: weights const {0.40,0.35,0.25}, role const `primary`, live_eligible const true, shadow_only const false), `shadowComparisonProfile` (theme_plus/theme_aggressive: role const `shadow_comparison`, live_eligible const false, shadow_only const true; weights stay open as priors), `themeOffProfile` (theme_off: weights const {0.6154,0.0,0.3846}, role const `attribution_baseline_and_rollback_anchor`, live const false, shadow const true); `min_comparison_weeks` const 12. All four Codex mutation cases now fail schema validation (shadow flipped live / balanced weight drift / non-proportional theme_off / weeks<12). **Repair 2 (calibration routing)**: split the collapsed `calibration_item_id=28` into `primary_weight_calibration_item_id=1` (§13.1 #1 = primary 40/35/25 weight prior) + `comparison_profile_calibration_item_id=28` (§13.1 #28 = comparison-profile weights + min comparison weeks), schema-required + const-pinned; updated preset + README. Added negative SCHEMA tests asserting `jsonschema.ValidationError` for shadow-flipped-live / balanced-weight-drift / theme_off-non-proportional / weeks<12 / balanced-flipped-shadow + a calibration-routing test; kept the positive preset validation + the cross-field invariant tests (theme_plus/aggressive sum-to-one + theme ordering, which draft-07 cannot express). Verify: scoring-profile schema tests 15 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2867 OK (zero regression; +6 net); the four named schema mutations now rejected; BOM/FFFD=0 (Chinese UTF-8); `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; no provider/broker/fetch. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 slice 1b trades `suggested_action` vocabulary drift. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-TRADE-ACTION-VOCAB-DRIFT`; severity `P1` (manual execution-log / schema-contract integrity before downstream live-normalized evidence consumption). Scope reviewed: full current dirty-tree review of US-short batch 1 slice 1b after slice 1a commit `531d4365`, including `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `tests/test_us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `schemas/examples/us_short_account_state_csv/trades.csv`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §3.6/§9/§12/§18.1, and route/privacy/test boundaries.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-TRADE-ACTION-VOCAB-DRIFT`): slice 1b claims `trades.csv.suggested_action` uses the §9 Chinese `final_action` vocabulary, but the implementation does not accept the design's exact non-fill value `否决/避开`. Evidence: `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §9 lists `final_action` as `建仓` / `加仓` / `减仓` / `清仓-止损` / `清仓-止盈` / `清仓-事件` / `持有` / `观察` / `否决/避开`; the changed route row also says `suggested_action` equals the §9 Chinese final_action vocab. In `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `TRADE_NOFILL_ACTIONS = ("持有", "观察", "否决")`, so `TRADE_ACTIONS` omits `否决/避开`. Independent probe: `reconcile_trades_positions([{suggested_action="否决/避开", executed="FALSE", fill_price="", fill_shares="", skip_reason="avoid"}], ...)` raises `[FATAL] ... must be one of ... '否决'`, while the non-design alias `否决` is accepted. The current tests cover invalid English `buy` and executed `持有`, but do not cover the complete §9 action set or the `否决/避开` edge.

Materiality: `trades.csv` is the private manual actual / execution-log input for later reconciliation and live-normalized evidence. A user following the system design or a future weekly report that emits the documented §9 value `否决/避开` will fail conversion even though the row is contract-valid. Conversely, accepting `否决` without documenting it as an alias creates a second hidden vocabulary and weakens the no-dangling / schema-first boundary that batch 1 is meant to establish.

Preferred repair is to accept the design-exact `否决/避开` as the canonical non-fill action; if `否决` is intentionally kept as a user-input alias, document that alias explicitly and test both the canonical value and alias behavior without changing the stored action silently. Update `trades.csv` template / README wording only if the canonical vocabulary is deliberately changed in the design. Boundary: converter, tests, CSV example, route docs, and this register only; do not implement batch 3 ship-gate evidence consumption, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, A-share crossing, short-selling support, or live trading.
