RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 slice 1a manual CSV accepts unknown columns and silently drops them. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-UNKNOWN-CSV-COLUMNS-SILENT-DROP`; severity `P1` (manual account-state contract integrity / future weekly sizing input; can misstate holding direction before any consumer gets a chance to validate it). Scope reviewed: full first-slice re-review of the current dirty US-short account-state implementation, including `runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, account-state and lineage schemas/examples/templates, tests, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `.gitignore` private-path behavior, and this register. The previous four account-state Required repairs are verified closed in the working tree: no in-repo nonprivate override, validator rejects impossible/future dates, register boundary is current, and cash must be `<= bucket`.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-UNKNOWN-CSV-COLUMNS-SILENT-DROP`): the converter only checks that required CSV columns exist; it does not reject unknown columns in either the CSV reader path or the pure `build_account_state` table path. Evidence: `_read_csv_table` builds `header`, checks `missing`, then returns stripped row dicts without checking extras (`runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py` lines 317-324). `_build_account_fields` and `_build_positions` then consume only known keys and ignore the rest (lines 198-231). Independent probe: a `positions.csv` row with extra `direction=short` and an `account.csv` row with extra `unexpected_account_flag` are accepted by `main`, and the output position becomes `{"direction": "long", ...}`; the pure `build_account_state` path accepts the same extra keys as well.

Materiality: slice 1a is the manual account-state contract that future US-short weekly holding re-evaluation and sizing will consume. The design says positions.csv has the fixed fields `ticker / shares / avg_cost_usd / entry_date / current_stop / notes`, v1 is long-only with `direction=long` as a marked door, and malformed/out-of-contract input must fail fast rather than silently degrade. If a user tries to record a short/borrowed position by adding `direction=short`, or adds an unsupported account/sizing field, the converter silently drops that fact and emits a long position. That can make the future report treat a short exposure as a long holding; tests currently cover schema additionalProperties only after JSON is produced, not unknown CSV headers before production.

Required repair: make the input contract strict before this slice can pass. Reject any unknown CSV header for `account.csv` and `positions.csv` (including row overflow represented by `None` keys from `csv.DictReader`), and reject unknown keys in the pure `build_account_state` table path too so tests/future callers cannot bypass the CSV gate. Keep the allowed optional columns (`portfolio_total_equity` for account; `current_stop` and `notes` for positions) and all current valid templates green. Add adversarial tests for at least: positions extra `direction=short` rejected; account extra unknown field rejected; CSV row with too many cells rejected; pure table path extra key rejected. Boundary: account-state converter/schema-doc wording/tests/register only; do not implement slice 1b trades reconciliation, short-channel support, provider calls, DataHub, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — I had applied the design's fail-fast principle to VALUES (anti-Excel-coercion) but not to STRUCTURE (columns/keys), so an out-of-contract column (e.g. `direction=short`, which v1 long-only would silently emit as long) was dropped. Added `EXPECTED_COLUMNS` (allowed = required + optional: account = the six §3.6 fields incl. optional `portfolio_total_equity`; positions = ticker/shares/avg_cost_usd/entry_date + optional current_stop/notes) and `_reject_unknown_columns` (rejects any column not in the allowed set, and treats the `csv.DictReader` `None` restkey — row-overflow cells — as unknown). Enforced on BOTH paths: `_read_csv_table` rejects an unknown CSV header (catches header-level extras even for a 0-row CSV) and `build_account_state` rejects unknown row keys (covers the pure-dict caller path + the `None` restkey from a too-many-cells row, so neither the CSV gate nor the pure path is a bypass). Tests: `test_positions_extra_direction_column_rejected` (the named short case), `test_account_extra_unknown_column_rejected`, `test_pure_path_extra_key_rejected`, `test_main_rejects_unknown_csv_column` (CSV header), `test_main_rejects_row_with_too_many_cells` (None restkey). Class-complete (pre-Codex checklist A — cover the malformed-structure / silent-drop CLASS, not just the named instance): also reject a duplicate CSV header (`csv.DictReader` keeps only the last same-named column, silently dropping the other column's data) — `_read_csv_table` raises on dupes, `test_main_rejects_duplicate_header`. The committed templates / happy path stay green (their columns are exactly the allowed set). RESOLVED P1 (2026-06-20): US-short batch 1 slice 1a account-state cash/bucket ceiling gap. status `resolved`(working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; pending Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`); Required ID `R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-CASH-BUCKET-CEILING-GAP`; severity `P1` (capital-policy / cross-bucket cash isolation before the weekly sizing consumer exists). Scope reviewed: current dirty tree for US-short account-state slice (`runners/us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py`, `schemas/us_short_account_state.schema.json`, lineage schema/examples/templates/tests, `docs/README.md`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, and this register). The previous three account-state Required repairs are verified closed in the working tree: no in-repo nonprivate override surface remains, validator rejects impossible/future dates, and the register boundary now distinguishes original docs-only landing from current slice 1a code.

Finding (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-CASH-BUCKET-CEILING-GAP`): `build_account_state` and `validate_account_state` accept `us_short_available_cash` greater than the computed `us_short_bucket_capital`. Independent probe: `us_market_equity=30000` produces `us_short_bucket_capital=10000`, but `us_short_available_cash=50000` builds and validates successfully (`cash_gt_bucket=ACCEPTED {"cash": 50000.0, "bucket": 10000.0}`). The schema only enforces cash `>= 0`; the validator only enforces `bucket == us_market_equity/3`, unique tickers, long-only, and date/PIT validity.

Materiality: this account-state schema is the future weekly sizing input, and the project-level capital policy says each market is split into 1/3 long / 1/3 short / 1/3 liquidity, A/US cash is non-fungible, and each runner must have a capital ceiling not exceeding its bucket. The US-short design also says the short bucket is computed from `us_market_equity/3`, and global cash allocation later consumes available cash. Accepting an account state where bucket-local cash exceeds the bucket can silently mix US-long / liquidity cash into US-short sizing unless every future consumer re-caps the field defensively. The safer contract is to reject the inconsistent state at the manual-input boundary.

Resolution (Claude `修复` 2026-06-20, working tree; 用户 `修复` 即授权; status `resolved` until Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`): judged valid and accepted — bucket-local cash exceeding the bucket would let US-long / liquidity cash silently mix into US-short sizing (capital policy: per-market 1/3 buckets, A/US cash non-fungible, runner ceiling <= its bucket). Enforced `us_short_available_cash <= us_short_bucket_capital` at BOTH boundaries: `build_account_state` rejects it at CSV build (after computing bucket) and `validate_account_state` rejects it too (so a hand-edited / non-builder JSON is caught by the single-source gate); both use the `_REL_EPS * max(1, bucket)` tolerance so `cash == bucket` (a fully-cash bucket) is allowed and only a meaningful excess is rejected. The schema description of `us_short_available_cash` now documents the cross-field invariant. Tests: `test_cash_exceeds_bucket_fatal` (build), `test_cash_equals_bucket_ok` (boundary positive control), `test_cash_exceeds_bucket_rejected_by_validator` (validator). Scope of the invariant (deliberate): only `cash <= bucket` is enforced (cash is part of the bucket). A `sum(positions avg_cost_usd * shares) + cash <= bucket` check is NOT added, because `avg_cost_usd` is a cost basis, not current market value, and the bucket is a forward capital allocation — that stricter check would falsely reject legitimately appreciated holdings; the runner-level sizing ceiling against current value belongs to the future weekly sizing consumer, not the manual-input contract. B-ripple caught + fixed: the pre-existing `test_bucket_is_equity_over_three` used equity=1000 (bucket≈333) with the default cash 4000, which the new invariant correctly rejected, so that test's cash was lowered to 100. Verify: account-state converter+schema+doc/route guards 87 OK; full discover `python -m unittest discover -s tests` 2826 OK in a runtime with jsonschema/requests/tushare (zero regression; +3 net) — full discover can be RED in a dependency-light runtime due to unrelated A-short requests/tushare imports + `pro=None`, which is environmental, not this slice; `py_compile` OK; `git diff --check` clean except CRLF; BOM/FFFD=0; no provider/broker/market-fetch introduced. Closure on Codex re-`审查 PASS` + 用户 `提交`.

Required repair: enforce the account-state capital invariant before this slice can pass: `us_short_available_cash <= us_short_bucket_capital` (within a small numeric tolerance) in both the CSV builder path and `validate_account_state`, so hand-edited JSON is also rejected. If the implementer believes a different model is needed, split the meaning explicitly (for example, raw account cash vs bucket-local deployable cash) and ensure the field consumed by future US-short sizing is capped to the bucket; do not keep the current ambiguous accepted state. Add builder-level and validator-level tests proving cash above bucket is rejected, keep zero cash valid, and update schema/docs wording if needed so the contract is clear. Boundary: account-state schema/converter/tests/docs/register only; do not implement slice 1b trades reconciliation, provider calls, DataHub consumption, broker/order automation, market fetch, paper/live evidence, or ship-gate changes.

Finding 1 (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-PRIVATE-OUTPUT-OVERRIDE-BYPASS`, severity P0 security / private-account hygiene): the new converter's fail-closed path guard can be bypassed for an in-repo non-gitignored output by passing `--allow-nonprivate-account-out`. Evidence: `_reject_nonprivate_account_output_path` returns before `git check-ignore` enforcement when `allow_nonprivate=True`, the CLI exposes that flag, and `tests/test_us_short_account_state_from_manual_tables.py::PrivacyGuardTests::test_allow_override_ok` locks the bypass in as a passing behavior. This conflicts with `docs/us_short_system_design.md` §11.6 / §18.1 #1, which says private outputs inside the repo and not ignored must fail-fast by `git check-ignore` truth, and it can write holdings / cash / cost into a tracked path such as `docs/*.json`.

Required repair 1: remove the in-repo nonprivate override, or restrict any deliberate export escape hatch to paths outside the repo only. In-repo non-gitignored paths must fail regardless of CLI flags. Replace the current positive override test with planted failures that prove an in-repo tracked path is rejected even if the flag is supplied; keep positive controls for outside-repo output and gitignored `state/us_short/*.json` output. Update CLI help/docstrings/SESSION_LOG wording accordingly.

Finding 2 (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-VALIDATOR-PIT-DATE-GAP`, severity P1 PIT / schema-contract): `validate_account_state` is documented as the single source of truth for `us_short_account_state` validity, but it accepts impossible and future dates if they arrive in an existing JSON state. Independent probe results: mutating a schema-valid state to `positions[0].entry_date=20260701` while `as_of=20260622` returned `PASSED`; mutating `entry_date=20260631` returned `PASSED`; mutating `as_of=20260631` and validating with that same `as_of` returned `PASSED`. The builder rejects these CSV inputs, but future consumers or hand-edited JSON could pass the validator and leak PIT-invalid account state downstream.

Required repair 2: make `validate_account_state` re-parse `state["as_of"]` and every `positions[*].entry_date` as real calendar dates, require `state["as_of"] == run as_of`, and require every entry date `<= state["as_of"]`. Add validator-level tests for future entry dates, impossible entry dates, and impossible `as_of` dates; do not rely only on builder-input tests.

Finding 3 (`R-USSHORT-ACCTSTATE-REGISTER-BOUNDARY-DRIFT`, severity P2 route-doc / cross-LLM continuity): the current register update adds batch 1 slice 1a progress stating that the account-state converter / guard is built, but the next paragraph still says the landing boundary is "docs + `.gitignore` only" and that "No US-short schema / runner ... is introduced." In the current working tree, US-short schema files and a runner are introduced. The old sentence was true for the prior docs-only landing, but after inserting current progress above it, the active Hot Queue entry now contains an adjacent contradiction.

Finding 1 (P1 / execution correctness + false contract): an active top-500 symbol with no SW industry-membership row makes `assemble_forward_inputs` ABORT, not gracefully exclude. Evidence: `forward_scored_items` (`data_layer.py` ~146) calls `base.industry_context_for_symbol`; the frozen function (`a_long_full_main_board_signal_search.py` ~822-825) RAISES `ValueError: active investable symbol has no industry membership source` when `industry_source=="missing"` (zero membership rows) and the symbol is active — it only returns `industry_excluded=True` for `no_interval_membership` or `exception_symbols`. Independent probe reproduced the abort for one active name with empty `index_member_records`. The data-layer docstring (~98-100) claims "缺成员的票 industry_context 标 excluded → 零误纳", which is FALSE. Materiality: the layer bypasses `base.load_industry_records`'s SW-repair supplement; the frozen full-main-board run needed per-symbol SW supplementation for 1189/3200 active names (`docs/a_long_main_board_sw_coverage_repair_execution_summary_20260604.json`), so bulk membership does not cover most names → the first real capture (`as_of>=20260630`) is at material risk of aborting on the first top-500 name lacking a membership row. Required repair: handle missing membership per the frozen contract — route missing-membership symbols into `exception_symbols` (so the frozen fn returns `industry_excluded=True`), or explicitly skip/exclude items with `industry_source=="missing"` in the data layer; fix the false docstring; do NOT rely on the frozen fn to "mark excluded" for `missing`. Also carry the frozen `industry_excluded` 4th return value onto each scored item (currently discarded at `data_layer.py` ~146) so `add_industry_neutral_scores` parity holds if `exception_symbols` ever non-empty (today hardcoded `frozenset()`).

Finding 2 (P1 / data contract / classification axis): `build_forward_context` (`data_layer.py` ~114-116) sets `active_symbols`/`delisted_symbols` from `delist_date is None` / `is not None`, but the frozen `base.build_signal_context` (~499-541) derives them from `stock_basic` list_status (`L` vs `D`). A still-trading `L`-status name with a FUTURE `delist_date` is `active` in the frozen contract but lands in `delisted_symbols` here. Probe: `delist_date=20251231`, `as_of=20240628` → `active=[]`, `delisted=[600000.SH]` (wrong). `active_symbols` feeds the Finding-1 missing-membership branch, so the mis-axis interacts with the abort path. Latent today (most L rows have empty delist_date) but a real divergence. Required repair: classify active/delisted by security-master origin (L vs D set), not by `delist_date is None`; `fetch_forward_panel` already separates `basic_l`/`basic_d` then merges and loses the distinction — thread the origin through.

Finding 3 (P2 material-for-first-run / provider contract): `fetch_forward_panel` calls `pro.index_member_all(ts_code=symbol, ...)` per symbol and a lineage guard asserts each row's `ts_code == symbol`, but the frozen materialization pulls SW membership via one BULK `index_member_all` (fields only, no ts_code filter) and the constituent stock may live in a separate field (Tushare `index_member_all` ts_code conventionally filters by INDEX code, constituent in `con_code`). If so, the per-symbol filter + lineage assertion + `industry_records_by_symbol` grouping (all assuming `ts_code==stock`) raise or mis-group at first real call. The "现写现验" provider-shape risk, but the most fragile call in the plan. Required repair: verify the real `index_member_all` route/params/field at first capture; prefer the bulk pull keyed on the constituent field; relax the per-symbol lineage guard accordingly.

Scope manifest: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` showed `M docs/SESSION_LOG.md`, `M runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py`, `M tests/test_a_long_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py`, `?? runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_data_layer.py`, `?? tests/test_a_long_value_yield_forward_paper_data_layer.py`; no staged files. This review covered the current A-long forward-paper full batch (`brain + lean top-500 data layer + run_forward_capture/main`) and did not review A-short, US lanes, real provider calls, capture execution, singleton-ledger spending, production readiness, or ship-gate evidence.

Finding 1 (P1 / data integrity / PIT frozen snapshot): `build_cohort_snapshot()` records `entry_date` for each frozen cohort construction, but `backfill_cohort()` recomputes the entry date from the current `trade_dates` on every backfill. Evidence: `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py::build_cohort_snapshot` sets `entry_date = _first_trade_day_after(as_of, trade_dates)` and stores it; `backfill_cohort()` later sets a fresh `entry_date = _first_trade_day_after(as_of, trade_dates)` and uses that derived index. Materiality: a forward-paper cohort's entry anchor is part of the frozen monthly snapshot. If a later calendar source or price-cache date set changes, historical cohorts can be re-anchored silently, contaminating OOS evidence while still passing tests and accumulator validation. Required repair: `backfill_cohort()` must use the saved cohort construction `entry_date` as the anchor, validate that it is present when `entry_status == "ok"`, validate it is in `trade_dates`, and fail-closed or explicitly mark unbackfillable if a recomputed first-open date disagrees with the frozen entry. Add adversarial tests for a shifted `trade_dates` list / stored-entry mismatch and a positive test for stable frozen-entry backfill.

Finding 2 (P1 / return lineage / delist and missing-exit semantics): `base.compute_return()` returns the actual benchmark exit date after `resolve_return_dates()` handles scheduled exit, `terminal_last_trade_before_delist`, and `next_available_after_missing_scheduled_exit`, but the new `backfill_cohort()` discards those returned dates and always records the scheduled `trade_dates[exit_idx]` with `exit_policy = "scheduled_exit_basket_equal_weight"`. Evidence: `runners/a_long_full_main_board_signal_search.py::resolve_return_dates` has non-scheduled exit policies; `compute_return()` returns `(stock_return, benchmark_return, entry_date, benchmark_exit_date)`; `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py::backfill_cohort` assigns `_e, _x` then writes scheduled exit metadata. Materiality: delist, halt, missing scheduled close, or terminal last-trade outcomes are central A-long data-integrity and survivorship risks. Recording them as ordinary scheduled exits makes the accumulator look cleaner than the actual evidence path. Required repair: preserve actual exit metadata from the frozen return resolver. At minimum, record the actual exit date used for the basket; if basket members use mixed exit policies/dates, encode a fail-closed or explicit mixed/member-audit policy rather than labeling the whole basket as scheduled. Add tests covering terminal delist / missing scheduled exit and the legal scheduled case.

Finding 3 (P1 / provider/data contract / execution gate): `fetch_forward_panel()` directly calls live Tushare endpoints without the call-plan protections used by prior A-long materialization slices: no explicit `start_date`/`end_date` on per-symbol fundamentals/prices/benchmark, no minimum-field validation before assembly, no pacing/budget envelope, no raw-payload or no-raw tracked-summary boundary, and no kwargs assertions in tests. Evidence: the new data layer calls `pro.cashflow(ts_code=...)`, `pro.income(ts_code=...)`, `pro.daily(ts_code=...)`, `pro.adj_factor(ts_code=...)`, `pro.index_daily(ts_code=...)`, `pro.index_member_all()`, `pro.namechange(...)`, and `pro.trade_cal(...)` with mostly fields-only args; the older A-long materialization packet records date windows, minimum fields, and `NetworkPacer` boundaries. Materiality: the prereg requires monthly PIT pulls, frozen top-500 universe, real delist/halt/merger outcomes, and separate user authorization before each fetch. A loose live-fetch wrapper can pull provider defaults, incomplete windows, or malformed fields and still assemble a seemingly valid paper accumulator. Required repair: add a narrow forward-capture call-plan contract for this lean slice: explicit date windows sufficient for TTM and all open horizons/backfill price history, minimum fields per endpoint, call count/budget, pacing or documented no-pacing decision, raw/gitignored or no-raw tracked summary policy, and tests asserting the fake provider receives those kwargs and that missing required fields fail before accumulator write.

Finding 4 (P2 / execution guard / output routing): `main()` help says `--as-of` is month-end `>= 20260630` and `--out` is an accumulator path under `research/results/...`, but the runner does not enforce these constraints before `run_forward_capture()` writes. Evidence: `runners/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_capture.py::main` defines help text for `--as-of` and `--out`, then initializes Tushare and calls `run_forward_capture()`; `write_accumulator()` writes to the supplied output path after schema/consistency validation only. Materiality: this is lower than the backfill/data-contract issues because the runner still requires both confirmation flags and remains research-only, but it can create a paper artifact for a non-month-end date or outside the intended research path. Required repair: add fail-closed guards for `as_of >= 20260630`, month-end-open decision semantics where feasible from the fetched calendar / trade dates, and a research-only output path rule or explicit refusal of production `result/` paths. Add tests for bad `as_of`, bad out path, and legal research path.

OPEN P1 (2026-06-19): A-long large-cap value-yield forward-paper accumulator schema promotion gate gap. Required ID `R-ALONG-VY-FP-ACCUMULATOR-SCHEMA-PROMOTION-GATE-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master dcb33dd 2026-06-19); severity `P1`; scope reviewed: `schemas/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_accumulator.schema.json`, `schemas/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking.schema.json`, `research/preregistrations/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_20260609.json`, `research/ledgers/a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_program_test_budget_ledger_20260609.json`, `tests/schema/test_a_long_large_cap_value_yield_forward_paper_tracking_schema.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-long value-yield forward PAPER / accumulator schema / promotion-read gate / no best-of-three / monthly capture artifact`.

Finding: the new untracked accumulator schema is syntactically valid JSON and passes `Draft7Validator.check_schema()`, but it does not enforce the frozen forward-paper decision contract strongly enough. Independent jsonschema probes showed the schema accepts an accumulator with `paper_read.matured_cohort_count=0`, `read_available=false`, and `routing="promote_eligible_pending_new_reviewed_real_money_prereg"`. The same accepted artifact also marks `cash_flow_to_circ_mv` as `primary_promotion_construction` in `construction_metrics`, even though the reviewed prereg freezes only `value_yield_composite_cf_sales` as promotion-eligible. A second accepted artifact includes a cohort before the `20260630` start floor, `interim_horizons_trading_days=[999]`, horizon key `"999"`, `basket_size=20` with `selected_symbols=[]`, and a `matured` horizon with `relative_excess_net=null` / no exit date.

Materiality: this is not a data-fetch or runner execution bug yet; the file is currently untracked and no capture runner is present. It is still material because this schema is the future official accumulator contract for a forward-paper promotion-read artifact. If committed as-is, a future runner or hand-built artifact could claim promotion eligibility with insufficient cohorts, wrong primary construction, malformed baskets, or non-matured return evidence while still passing schema validation. That weakens the reviewed anti-best-of-three / single-primary / paper-only governance from the 20260609 prereg and could misroute a later real-money forward-live prereg decision.

Required repair: tighten the accumulator schema and add adversarial schema tests. At minimum: enforce exactly the three construction IDs where applicable; bind `promotion_role` to `construction_id` so only `value_yield_composite_cf_sales` can be `primary_promotion_construction` and the two single yields are diagnostic only; constrain interim horizon list and horizon property names to the frozen set (`21`, `63`, `126`, `252`, `504` as applicable); reject `routing=promote_eligible...` unless `read_available=true`, primary matured cohorts meet the 12-cohort minimum, and persistence/drawdown booleans are true; reject `insufficient_cohorts` when the read says enough cohorts; require matured horizon records to have numeric `relative_excess_net` and concrete exit metadata; prevent pre-start-floor cohorts; require selected symbol uniqueness and consistency with `basket_size` or a documented status-specific zero-basket shape; pin required source refs for prereg, ledger, batch execution summary, and schema/design refs. Add planted-failure tests for each of the accepted bad probes above plus positive tests for legal pending and legal matured artifacts.

Boundary: do not fetch data, run capture, spend the singleton ledger, change the frozen prereg construction, change thresholds/horizons/benchmarks/universe, promote a single-factor view, claim alpha validation, production readiness, ship-gate evidence, real-money readiness, full-size use, DataHub readiness, or broker/order automation in this repair. This is a schema/test repair only unless separately approved.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-19): A-short S3b R4b ratchet invariant guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R4B-RATCHET-INVARIANT-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 9e5c10c 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-short S3b R4b / machine.ratchet / ratcheted_stop null / effective-stop invariant / save envelope`.

Finding: the previous duplicate-key sidecar read gap is addressed in the current working tree: `load_holding_ratchet()` now rejects duplicate `(ts_code, entry_date)` before dict folding and rejects row `last_as_of > envelope as_of`. The remaining material gap is the in-report ratchet invariant. `_ratchet_report_error()` says `ratcheted_stop` must be at least the current-week effective stop (`max(S3a plan.stop, R4a breakeven)`), but its check is `if eff and _is_finite_num(rs) and rs < max(eff)`, so `ratcheted_stop=None` skips the comparison. Independent probe built a held M6.7 report with `machine.entry_exit_size_star.plan.stop=3.05` and `machine.ratchet.ratcheted_stop=None`; both `validate_m67_consistency()` and official `write_m67_report()` accepted it (`write_m67_ratchet_null_stop=ACCEPTED plan_stop=3.05`). Same-class writer note: `save_holding_ratchet()` also accepted a state row with `last_as_of=20991231` while writing envelope `as_of=20260617`; a later `load_holding_ratchet()` rejects the file, but the writer still creates a corrupted sidecar despite the schema description saying load/save enforce the envelope.

Materiality: normal `_apply_holding_ratchet()` currently computes a finite `ratcheted_stop` when the current report has a finite S3a stop or R4a breakeven, so this is not a normal happy-path output bug. It is still material because R4b is a cross-week holding-state contract and `write_m67_report()` is the official write boundary. A hand-built report or future builder drift can hide the protective ratchet stop as `null` even though the current-week stop exists, weakening the "ratchet contains current week effective stop / only-up stop" invariant that downstream review and the user-facing report rely on. The save-time envelope gap is a fail-closed/documentation mismatch: it will be caught on the next load, but it should not be written by the sidecar writer in the first place.

Required repair: strengthen `_ratchet_report_error()` so when current-week effective stop exists, `ratcheted_stop` must be a finite number and `>= max(effective_stop)`; `None` / non-finite must raise. Keep `ratcheted_stop=None` legal only when there is no finite S3a stop, no finite R4a breakeven, and no finite prior ratcheted stop. Add adversarial tests proving `validate_m67_consistency()` and `write_m67_report()` reject `ratcheted_stop=None` when `plan.stop` exists, while the legal no-effective-stop null case still passes if expected by design. Add a save-time PIT envelope guard in `save_holding_ratchet()` for row `last_as_of <= as_of` (or narrow the schema/docstring claim if the design intentionally relies on load-only rejection), with a direct writer test.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-19): A-short S3b R4b ratchet sidecar duplicate-key PIT bypass. Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R4B-RATCHET-SIDECAR-DUPLICATE-PIT-BYPASS`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 9e5c10c 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `.gitignore`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-short S3b R4b / holding ratchet sidecar / duplicate key / future-state guard bypass`.

Finding: R4b correctly adds a gitignored private sidecar route and normal builder tests pass for bootstrap, re-entry, same-week idempotence, future `last_as_of` rejection, only-up stop, only-up disposition, and render. The material gap is in sidecar read validation. `schemas/a_short_holding_ratchet.schema.json` says `(ts_code, entry_date)` rows are unique, and `load_holding_ratchet()` says it validates the sidecar to prevent damaged / hand-edited state. But `load_holding_ratchet()` returns a dict comprehension keyed by `ts_code|entry_date`, so duplicate rows silently overwrite earlier rows before `_apply_holding_ratchet()` checks `last_as_of > as_of`. Independent probe created a schema-valid sidecar with two rows for `600000.SH|20260601`: first row `last_as_of=20991231`, second row `last_as_of=20260610`. `load_holding_ratchet()` kept only the second row, and `_apply_holding_ratchet(..., as_of=20260617)` accepted the state instead of rejecting the hidden future row.

Materiality: normal `save_holding_ratchet()` currently writes from a dict, so ordinary system output is unique. This is still material because R4b is a cross-week PIT state file. A damaged, manually edited, merge-conflicted, or future-writer sidecar can hide future state behind a later duplicate row and bypass the very guard intended to prevent future-contaminated ratchet decisions. Since the sidecar contains real holding state and feeds future weekly reports, read-time corruption must fail closed.

Required repair: make the sidecar reader/writer fail closed on duplicate identity and PIT envelope corruption. At minimum, `load_holding_ratchet()` must iterate rows, compute `_holding_ratchet_key(ts_code, entry_date)`, and raise on any duplicate key before returning the dict. Add an adversarial test where a duplicate key hides a future `last_as_of` row and assert load/apply rejects it. Prefer also checking row `last_as_of <= top-level as_of` at load time and adding a schema/runtime note that composite uniqueness is enforced in Python, not JSON schema draft-07.

Boundary: do not change R4b only-up math, re-entry semantics, same-week idempotence, R4a price-cross / breakeven logic, S3a price formulas, `table.损` / `plan.stop`, `操作` enum, EGS / TopN / selection / share-size / hard-veto behavior, broker/order behavior, provider calls, or sidecar privacy route without separate approval. Keep `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json` excluded from commit.

OPEN P2 (2026-06-19): A-short S3b R3 explicit-null price no-dangling guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-R3-EXPLICIT-NULL-PRICE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 8869e8d 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; untracked excluded byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short S3b R3 / held advisory prices / explicit-null no-dangling / validator field-presence guard`.

Finding: S3b R3 correctly extends normal builder output for held rows: `clear_review` writes `table.清仓价 == S3a plan.stop`, `reduce_review` writes `table.减仓价 == S3a plan.t1` plus `table.减仓比例 == "1/3"`, and schema/render can display those advisory fields. The material gap is in write-time validation when the referenced S3a price is unavailable (`plan.t1 is None` for breached reduce, or `plan is None` for no-price clear). `validate_m67_consistency()` compares with `tbl.get(...)` / `mc.get(...)`, so it treats an omitted field and an explicit `null` as equivalent. Independent probes accepted: (1) a breached `reduce_review` held report after deleting `table.减仓价` and `machine.reduce_price` while keeping `减仓比例="1/3"`; (2) a no-price `clear_review` held report after deleting `table.清仓价` and `machine.clear_price`; (3) a non-held candidate report carrying `machine.reduce_price = null`.

Materiality: normal `_apply_holding_disposition()` currently emits explicit `null`, so this is not a normal builder-output failure. It is still material because R3's contract is explicitly no-dangling: when S3a cannot compute the advisory price, the user-visible output must say the price was not computed, not silently omit the field. The renderer only shows "未算出" when the table key exists. A future builder drift or hand-built report can therefore pass validation while hiding the missing reduce/clear price, and non-held rows can carry R3 machine fields despite the held-only claim.

Required repair: strengthen `validate_m67_consistency()` (or an equivalent write-time guard) to distinguish field absence from explicit `null`. For `clear_review`, require the `清仓价` table key and `machine.clear_price` key to be present, with value exactly `S3a plan.stop` (including explicit `None` when plan is absent/unavailable), and reject `减仓价` / `减仓比例` / reduce machine fields. For `reduce_review`, require the `减仓价`, `减仓比例`, `machine.reduce_price`, and `machine.reduce_ratio` keys to be present, with `减仓价 == S3a plan.t1` (including explicit `None`) and ratio equal to the advisory fixed档; reject `清仓价` / clear machine fields. For other held signals, reject any R3 table or machine field even when the value is `None`. For non-held rows, reject any R3 table or machine field by key presence, not only non-null values. Add adversarial tests for missing explicit null reduce price, missing explicit null clear price when plan is absent, missing machine null while table null exists, stray clear/reduce machine null on the wrong disposition, and non-held `machine.reduce_price = None`.

Boundary: do not change S3a price formulas, stop/t1/t2 semantics, `操作` enum, EGS / TopN / selection / share-size / hard-veto behavior, reducer/clear automatic actions, broker/order behavior, provider calls, R4 active-action / ratchet behavior, or the fixed advisory ratio without separate approval. Keep `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json` excluded from commit.

Required ID `R-ASHORT-S3B-HOLDING-DISPOSITION-SCOPE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` round-2 global guard + committed master 6a7ce92 2026-06-19); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_m67_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; PIT label `A-short S3b / holding disposition / holding-row scope / privacy-shape guard`.

Finding: S3b R1+R2 correctly adds visible `table.持仓处置` / `table.禁止加仓` for normal held reports, keeps candidate reports without those table columns, and renders the new held fields. The material gap is the write-time boundary: `_merge_holding_disposition()` and `validate_m67_consistency()` recompute from **all** `machine.operation_impact`, while the design and registry say the merge source is holding-side impact only (`holding_row_impact` / `existing_holding` / private held signal). `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()` also does not bind `forward_event_` held signals to holding/private shape. Independent probe: a held report carrying `source_field="forward_event_limit_unlock"` but shaped as `candidate_row_impact` / `impact_scope="new_entry"` / `privacy_class="public_tracked"` with `holding_effect="hold_watch"` and `blocked_add_required=true` is accepted after adding the visible required text; `_apply_holding_disposition()` sets `持仓处置=持有警戒` and `禁止加仓=True`, and `validate_m67_consistency()` accepts. A generic candidate-like impact can likewise drive `machine.holding_management_signal="clear_review"`.

Materiality: normal builder output currently appears correct, so this is not observed as a normal weekly artifact leak. It is still material because S3b is a held-only / private-account structure. A hand-built artifact or future builder drift can promote public/candidate-shaped evidence into a private held disposition, contaminating the new structure that downstream consumers are expected to trust. This repeats the same guard-vs-claim class caught in earlier 4.2 row-scope reviews.

Required repair: make S3b merge and validation fail closed on scope. Acceptable repair: `_merge_holding_disposition()` should only consume impacts that are valid held signals (`visibility_shape=="holding_row_impact"`, `impact_scope=="existing_holding"`, held/private privacy where applicable, and non-`none` `holding_effect` or `blocked_add_required`); or the validator should first reject any impact that tries to affect holding disposition without that shape. Add source-class guards for `forward_event_` held impacts so held rows require holding/private shape and non-held rows cannot carry holding effects. Also reject non-held reports carrying `machine.holding_management_signal` / `machine.blocked_add_required` without the held table fields. Add adversarial tests for wrong-shape `forward_event_`, generic candidate-like holding effect, and non-held machine-field leakage; keep the normal builder/render tests passing.

Finding: `_fin_pit_periods()` correctly drops non-PIT rows, including `income` / `balancesheet` realized reports whose `end_date > as_of`. But `_financial_trends()` marks a `(ts_code, statement_type)` as checked as soon as the provider returns any non-`None` list. The markdown renderer can then say the candidate financial statements were checked and had no red flags, even though there was no PIT-valid realized statement basis for that `(票, 报表类)`.

Required repair: distinguish "provider returned an empty list" from "provider returned rows but zero PIT-valid rows." For `income` / `balancesheet`, a non-empty provider result that leaves no PIT-valid realized periods must become per-key `unchecked_codes` or the whole section `unknown_or_unavailable`, not `checked` empty. Add adversarial tests for future-only `income` and `balancesheet` provider rows; keep legal true-empty provider `[]` as checked/no-red-flag, keep PIT-valid no-red-flag rows checked empty, and keep forecast future `end_date` allowed.

Finding: the implementation direction is acceptable in purpose. `normalize_candidate()` passes existing `fundamental.profitability` / `fundamental.quality` / `scores.l2_flags` into `financial_quality`; `_financial_quality_operation_impacts()` emits a non-production advisory `operation_impact` only for red flags; `build_m67_report()` lands it in `精简结论区.风控触发`; and the current builder does not emit this impact for held positions. Because the current builder happens not to emit held financial_quality impacts, no normal-output leak was observed. OPEN P2 (2026-06-18): A-short 4.2 Round5 block_trade discount price coverage guard gap. Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-BLOCK-TRADE-DISCOUNT-PRICE-COVERAGE-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master d98db25e 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` decision 5 / 大宗交易折价率 requirement / comparison-only boundary; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / block_trade third cut / discount price evidence / field coverage / no-dangling`.

Finding: the discount direction is acceptable in purpose. The slice uses raw same-day close from `pro.daily`, keeps discount comparison-only, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / action / share size / veto / production effect. The material gap is coverage/no-dangling on the block-trade price side. `_fetch_block_trade()` requests `price`, but it still treats a response missing the `price` column as a successful checked fetch and returns rows with `price=None`. `_block_trade_events()` then emits `parties[].price=None`; `_attach_block_discount()` can set `discount_status="checked"` and add event `close`, while every party has `discount=None`. `validate_weekly_report()` accepts this because checked discount days only require `close` and a `discount` key, not explicit `price` evidence. The schema also leaves `parties[].price` optional, so a hand-built checked discount event with no price key can pass schema and validator.

Materiality: 4.2 requires each new external field to prove availability / reliability before use, and discount cannot be computed from close alone. A checked discount layer with missing block-trade price can render as `—` while still presenting the discount slice as checked. This is not a production-trading leak because the field remains comparison-only, but it creates false coverage evidence for the third-cut field and can hide provider/API shape drift.

Finding: the block_trade parties direction is acceptable in purpose: buyer/seller is added as same-endpoint enrichment, stays inside `block_trade.events[].parties`, renders a comparison-only buyer→seller column/text, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / table action / share size / veto / production effect. The gap is coverage/no-dangling. `_fetch_block_trade()` requests `buyer,seller` but only requires `ts_code` and `amount`; if the provider response lacks `buyer` / `seller` columns, it still returns a successful row with `buyer=None,seller=None`. `_block_trade_events()` then emits a checked event with parties `[{"buyer": null, "seller": null, ...}]`, and render / M6.7 text can show `?→?` while the report is still `status="checked"`. Separately, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json` leaves `events[].parties` optional, and `validate_weekly_report()` / `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()` accept a checked block_trade event with no `parties` at all. This contradicts the second-cut claim that buyer/seller parties are now the landed field.

Materiality: 4.2 requires each newly fetched data item to prove availability / quality before use, and every analysis field must have a real M6.7 landing or an explicit unknown path. The previous first-cut live note recorded `ts_code/trade_date/price/vol/amount`, not buyer/seller, so the current `SESSION_LOG` claim that buyer/seller was already seen by the first-cut probe is not supported by the durable log. This is not a production-trading leak because the field remains comparison-only, but it can falsely present the buyer/seller slice as checked when the actual buyer/seller fields are absent.

Required repair: tighten block_trade parties coverage in the current working tree. Acceptable repair: (1) make `_fetch_block_trade()` fail closed for the parties slice when `buyer` / `seller` columns are absent, or add an explicit parties coverage status / unknown path that does not render `?→?` as checked buyer/seller evidence; (2) enforce a write-time no-dangling rule for checked `block_trade.events`: if parties are part of the active second-cut schema, each event must carry `parties`, and `len(parties)` must match `trade_count`; each party must have explicit `buyer`, `seller`, and `amount` keys, while individual values may be null only when the provider column exists but the cell is blank; (3) add adversarial tests for missing buyer/seller columns, missing `parties`, and party-count mismatch, plus positive tests for legal parties and legal blank buyer/seller cells; (4) fix the top SESSION_LOG / comments claim so it does not say buyer/seller was verified in the first-cut live probe unless a separate user-approved `执行` actually verifies it.

Required ID `R-ASHORT-GAP42-ROUND5-TRADE-EVENT-COVERAGE-PRIVACY-GUARD-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 606bd225 2026-06-18); severity `P2`; scope reviewed: `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_phase5_engine.py`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `schemas/examples/a_short_gap_data_field_registry.example.json`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_a_short_gap_data_registry.py`, `docs/SESSION_LOG.md`; design source reviewed: `C:\Users\cnhea\Desktop\4.2.md` §5.3 / §10.3 / §11.5 / §12.2 / §13; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short 4.2 Round5 / block_trade first cut / dragon-list sibling guard / unknown-not-clear / holding privacy shape`.

Finding: the block_trade first-cut direction is acceptable in purpose: it stays analysis-only / comparison-only, uses gated `pro.block_trade`, writes a weekly `block_trade` section, lands row-level `block_trade_appearance` impacts, and does not change EGS / TopN / selection / action / sizing. However the write-time consumer guard is incomplete in the same class as the dragon-list guards it mirrors. Independent probes showed malformed reports are accepted: (1) `block_trade.status="checked"` with `window_dates=[]` and no events; (2) `block_trade.status="checked"` with every `window_dates` entry also in `unchecked_dates` and no events; (3) a held report with a `block_trade_appearance` impact mutated from `holding_row_impact/private_account` to `candidate_row_impact/public_tracked`; and the same three states are accepted for `dragon_list_appearance`. This means a report can claim a checked no-event state without any actually checked date, or carry a holding-related event impact with public/candidate shape, while `validate_weekly_report()` still passes. There is also active runner prose drift in the new block_trade comments/docstring that says non-candidate holdings are future work, while the actual implementation and registry claim the current slice covers `weekly.reports` (candidate plus account holdings).

Materiality: 4.2 requires unknown-not-clear for provider coverage and private handling for true account / holding information. The current builder normally emits the correct block_trade holding privacy shape, and `--account` output-path guard still protects normal private reports, so no tracked leak was observed. The material gap is the consumer/write-time contract: future builder drift or hand-constructed reports can pass validation with false coverage or public/candidate holding shape. This affects review quality and the final M6.7 artifact contract, especially because block_trade deliberately copied the dragon-list pattern and the sibling guard gap is already proven.

Required repair: tighten the trade-event write-time guard for both `block_trade` and sibling `dragon_list` in the current working tree. Acceptable repair:
(1) For each checked trade-event section, require `window_dates` to be non-empty and require at least one actually checked date (`window_dates - unchecked_dates` non-empty). A state where no dates were checked must be `unknown_or_unavailable`, not `checked`; reject checked-empty-window and checked-all-unchecked. Keep partial failure valid only when at least one date was checked.
(2) Enforce row privacy / visibility shape for trade-event impacts. If the report is a held position (`machine.stateful_risk.position_state == "held"`) and the impact source is `dragon_list_appearance` or `block_trade_appearance`, the impact must be `visibility_shape="holding_row_impact"`, `impact_scope="existing_holding"`, `new_entry_effect="none"`, and `privacy_class="private_account"` or stricter. Non-held rows must remain candidate/public shape. Do not rely only on registry tests.
(3) Add adversarial tests for block_trade and dragon_list: checked empty window rejected, checked all-unchecked rejected, held impact public/candidate mutation rejected, plus positive tests for a legal partial-unchecked state and a legal held private impact.
(4) Align active block_trade comments/docstrings with the actual current scope: first cut covers `weekly.reports` (candidate plus account holdings); buyer/seller seat analysis and discount-rate analysis are later, but non-candidate holding coverage is not later.

Add a focused registry test that fails if a row mentions account holdings / `holding_row_impact` / `private_account` behavior or has `operation_impact_target="both"` while still claiming only `public_tracked` or only `candidate_row_impact`. Keep the runtime comparison-only boundary unchanged unless a small wording update is necessary.

Finding: the second-cut direction is acceptable: `top_inst` stays comparison-only, does not create a new `operation_impact`, does not change EGS/TopN/selection/action/share size, and keeps true provider calls gated behind `--confirm`. The gap is the seat coverage contract. `validate_weekly_report()` only checks the forward case "if an event has `seats`, it must not be on an unchecked seat date"; it does not check the reverse case. Independent probes showed three malformed reports are accepted: (1) `dragon_list.seats_status="checked"` with an event that has no `seats` and no `unchecked_seat_dates`; (2) an event with `seats` but no `inst_net_buy`; (3) an event with `seats`/`inst_net_buy` but no `seats_status`. This lets the report claim the seat layer is checked while per-event seat evidence is missing or not governed by any coverage status. It violates 4.2's unknown-not-clear and no-dangling rules for new provider data.

Required repair: add a reverse seat coverage guard in `validate_weekly_report()` (or equivalent write-time guard). Acceptable invariant: if any event has `seats` or `inst_net_buy`, `dragon_list.seats_status` must be `checked`; if `seats_status=="checked"`, then every event whose `trade_date` is not in `unchecked_seat_dates` must carry a `seats` array and an explicit `inst_net_buy` key (value may be null); events on `unchecked_seat_dates` must not carry `seats`/`inst_net_buy`; if `seats_status=="unknown_or_unavailable"`, no event may carry `seats`/`inst_net_buy`; `unchecked_seat_dates` must stay inside `window_dates` and should only be meaningful with `seats_status=="checked"`. Add adversarial tests for all accepted bad cases above, plus positive tests for checked empty seats (`seats=[]`, `inst_net_buy=null`) and unchecked date without seats.

OPEN P1 (2026-06-18): Tushare health probe plaintext token / false-health diagnostic gap. Required ID `R-TUSHARE-HEALTH-PROBE-PLAINTEXT-TOKEN-AND-FALSE-OK-GAP`; status `resolved` (Codex re-`审查 PASS` + committed master 695b8621 2026-06-18; 实测真探针 [OK] 确认 weekly pinned 取数正常); severity `P1`; scope reviewed: untracked `runners/tushare_health_probe.py`; related current weekly path: `runners/a_short_iv_feed_probe.py::init_tushare_pro`, `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/materialize_execution_price_data_tushare.py`; excluded untracked byproduct `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`; PIT label `A-short infrastructure / Tushare health probe / token transport + false OK`.

Finding: the probe is useful in purpose, but unsafe and misleading as written. First, `_TUSHARE_HTTP_URL = "http://api.tushare.pro"` and the direct comparison posts `{"token": token, ...}` to that URL, so running the helper in a real environment can send `TUSHARE_TOKEN` over plaintext HTTP. Not printing the token is not enough; AGENTS security rules also forbid unsafe propagation of secrets. Second, package-path success is `bool(cols)`, so a response with columns but zero rows is treated as healthy. This contradicts the helper's own goal of catching package paths that silently return empty data. Third, the helper says A segment is the weekly true path, but it calls raw `ts.pro_api(token)` instead of reusing `runners.a_short_iv_feed_probe.init_tushare_pro()`, while the current weekly path pins the Tushare base URL before `pro_api`. The probe can therefore blame or clear the wrong layer.

Required repair: (1) never send the token to an `http://` endpoint; use an HTTPS endpoint consistent with the current pinned provider path, or skip the HTTP comparison unless HTTPS is proven. Add a no-network test/fake request capture that fails on non-HTTPS. (2) Define health as non-empty known-good rows plus required columns, not just columns. Add a fake dataframe regression where `columns` exist but `len(df)==0` returns nonzero and does not print a healthy verdict. (3) Make the A segment actually test the same weekly path by reusing `init_tushare_pro(token)`, or explicitly split the output into "raw unpinned package control" and "weekly pinned package path"; if it claims weekly path, it must use the pinned path and the same important fields for `share_float` and `disclosure_date`. Keep tests no-network and do not require a real token.

Boundary: no real Tushare call, no token logging, no new provider access, no data fetch, no weekly pipeline behavior change beyond the helper's import/reuse if needed, no commit of `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`. Do not run the live token probe until this Required is fixed and reviewed.

Finding: the new generalized `forward_event_` guard is one-way only. It checks that any `source_field` starting with `forward_event_` is advisory-only and that the user-facing advice contains the future-event marker, but it does not prove that the impact actually comes from a matching `upcoming_events.events[]` row. Independent Codex probes created a weekly report with `upcoming_events={"status":"checked","events":[]}` and manually inserted one row-level `operation_impact` plus the required advice marker. Three variants all passed `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()`, `validate_weekly_report()`, and `write_weekly_report()`: `source_field="forward_event_limit_unlock"`, `source_field="forward_event_earnings_disclosure"`, and `source_field="forward_event_fake"`. Materiality: desktop `4.2.md` requires forward events to be visible, PIT-safe, source-traceable, and no-dangling via `upcoming_events` -> row `operation_impact` / M6.7 surfaces. Current code can produce or accept a row saying "future event affects this stock" even when the calendar has no such event, or even when the event type is not supported. This is not a trading-action bug because the impact is still advisory-only, but it is a data-integrity / evidence-lineage bug in the M6.7 official output.

Required repair: add a reverse guard from row impact back to calendar evidence. Acceptable shape: in `validate_weekly_report()` (or an equivalent write-time guard), every row `machine.operation_impact[]` whose `source_field` starts with `forward_event_` must (1) have a source suffix that maps to an allowed `upcoming_events.events[].event_type` enum (`limit_unlock`, `earnings_disclosure`, and future types only after schema/metadata expansion); (2) have a matching checked calendar event with the same `ts_code` and `event_type`; (3) have `evidence_ref.value` aligned to that event type, for example `upcoming_events.events[earnings_disclosure]`; and (4) keep the existing analysis-only guard (`production_effect_enabled=false`, `veto_class=none`, no hard veto/rescue, no EGS/TopN/action-table change). Add adversarial tests for: fake source type rejected; legal source with no matching calendar event rejected; legal source for another code rejected; legal multi-type same-code events pass; checked-empty calendar with no forward impacts still passes. Do not solve this by deleting the marker guard; keep the user-visible advice guard as the second layer.

Boundary: no data fetch, no provider contact, no `pro.disclosure_date` live validation, no EGS / TopN / selection / table-action / production result change, no hard veto/rescue, no S3b automatic reduce/sell/add, no price formula, no broker/order behavior, no commit of `research/results/a_short/iv_feed_20260605/iv_feed.json`. This is a guard/test repair for the current analysis-only M6.7 forward-events slice.

Remaining material loopholes: (1) `R-ASHORT-GAP42-FORWARD-EVENTS-ROW-LANDING-GUARD-GAP` still includes a validator/landing gap beyond the manual-review-only holding case: a weekly artifact can contain a checked event for a `reports[]` code, skip `_attach_forward_event_impacts()`, and still pass `validate_weekly_report()` with `machine.operation_impact` absent. This means row no-dangling is done by the current `main()` order, not enforced by the consumer validator. (2) `R-ASHORT-GAP42-FORWARD-EVENTS-PARTIAL-UNKNOWN-GAP`: `_upcoming_events()` returns `status="checked", events=[]` when one code successfully returns `[]` and another code fails/returns `None`. (3) `R-ASHORT-GAP42-FORWARD-EVENTS-SOURCE-GUARD-GAP`: `validate_operation_impact_no_dangling()` has semantic-source isolation but no forward-event-source isolation. A generated `forward_event_limit_unlock` impact can be mutated to `veto_class="production_hard_veto"` and `production_effect_enabled=true` while keeping `new_entry_effect="manual_review"` and `操作="建仓"`; `validate_weekly_report()` still PASSes. Finding 1 (row landing / no-dangling gap): desktop `4.2.md` lines 276-281, 345, 741, and 770 require forward events to be analysis-only but still land in M6.7 as candidate/holding row impact: candidates can get `manual_review` / `priority_down` / `sizing_down` / `observe_required`; holdings can get `hold_watch` / `blocked_add_required` / `reduce_review` text; M6.7 landing includes `upcoming_events`, `风控触发`, `操作建议`, and when applicable `股数`. The implementation only sets `weekly["upcoming_events"]` as a global weekly object (`runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py` around `_exdiv_codes` / `_upcoming_events`) and renders one global Markdown section (`runners/a_short_m67_render.py` upcoming-events block). It does not attach the event to the affected `reports[]` row, does not create row-level `operation_impact`, and does not update the affected row's user-visible `风控触发` / `操作建议`. Independent Codex probe injected a valid `limit_unlock` for `600000.SH`; `validate_weekly_report()` accepted the weekly report, but the 600000.SH row had `row_operation_impact_sources=[]`, no `upcoming_events` / `limit_unlock` / `解禁` text in the row, `风控触发=="无"`, and `操作=="建仓"`. Materiality: the calendar is visible as a side table but is disconnected from the exact M6.7 decision row the user reads, so the field is dangling for the row-level risk/action contract.

Required repair for Finding 1: preserve the global `upcoming_events` index if useful, but also consume each checked event into the affected candidate/holding row's M6.7 surface. Minimum acceptable behavior: candidate rows with near `limit_unlock` show a user-visible event warning and an analysis-only row impact (`manual_review` / `observe_required` / `priority_down` / `sizing_down` as the reviewed mapping chooses) without becoming a production hard veto; holding rows show holding-scope warning text such as `hold_watch` / `blocked_add_required` / `reduce_review` text only, with no automatic sell/reduce action before S3b. The repair must keep `production_effect_enabled=false`, must not change EGS selection, TopN, production `result/a_short`, historical backtest, broker/order behavior, or price formulas. Add adversarial tests proving a valid event is visible on the exact candidate row and on the exact holding row, not only in a global section.

Finding 2 (mandatory guard tests missing): `4.2.md` line 741 explicitly requires `row no-dangling`, `PIT observed_at`, `unknown-not-clear`, `no-EGS/TopN-change`, and `no-hard-veto-rescue` tests for the forward_events first version. Materiality: the same slice claims "analysis-only / 不改 EGS·TopN·动作", but the required safety contract is not test-pinned; a future refactor could either leave events dangling again or accidentally turn them into production action.

Required repair for Finding 2: add tests that (a) fail if an `upcoming_events` item does not land in the matching M6.7 row surface, (b) compare report row set/order and candidate behavior with/without injected unlock events to prove no EGS/TopN change, and (c) prove a hard-veto candidate remains hard-vetoed and is not rescued by any positive/neutral event, while an event warning cannot become `production_hard_veto` or write production evidence. Keep tests no-network via injected providers / fixtures only.

Codex review finding for the A-short M6.7 Monday-intraday weekend-news window (2026-06-15; status `accepted_risk` (user explicitly accepted Monday-news inclusion on 2026-06-15; no code repair required for this boundary); severity `P2` documented operational semantics; scope `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `runners/weekly_screening.ps1`, `tests/test_a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, `schemas/a_short_weekly_report.schema.json`, `runners/a_short_m67_render.py`, `docs/a_short_weekly_pipeline_design_20260610.md`, current 20260612 weekly artifact diff, and exclusion review of untracked `research/results/a_short/em_probe_smoke_20260614/*`; PIT label `A-short M6.7 advisory / Monday before-close run / weekend-plus-Monday semantic-news clock`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-M67-WEEKEND-NEWS-WINDOW-GAP`): the current repair makes the M6.7 price clock explicit, while the semantic/news clock remains inclusive through Monday `as_of`. In `runners/a_short_weekly_pipeline.py`, both auto semantic providers are constructed with `args.as_of`: `_build_cninfo_semantic_provider(..., args.as_of, args.cninfo_lookback_days)` and `_build_deepseek_web_llm_provider(..., args.as_of, args.web_news_lookback_days)`. The downstream fetch windows are inclusive through `as_of`: `fetch_cninfo` sends `[as_of-lookback, as_of]`, and `_em_news_in_window` returns true for any `published_at` date `<= as_of`. A no-network AST probe against `_em_news_in_window` confirmed that with `as_of=20260615`, Saturday 2026-06-13, Sunday 2026-06-14, and Monday 2026-06-15 all return `True`. `runners/weekly_screening.ps1` also documents the live path as "新闻窗 as_of=周一 -> 判到周六/周日(及任何周一早间)", which now matches the accepted boundary after the user's 2026-06-15 follow-up. Accepted-risk disposition: no repair is required while Monday news is accepted. Codex review finding for the A-short EM news-feed feasibility probe draft (2026-06-14; status `resolved` (committed local master 2026-06-14 `ecf2b5d`, Codex `审查` PASS); severity `P2`; scope `runners/a_short_em_news_probe.py`, `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_em_news_probe_summary.schema.json`, `tests/test_a_short_em_news_probe.py`, `docs/a_short_semantic_risk_contract.md`, `docs/README.md`; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk / EM web_llm source-feasibility probe / fetcher-filter audit gap`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-EM-PROBE-FETCHER-FILTER-AUDIT-GAP`): the new EM probe is the right shape for replacing the deleted `_diag_web_sources.py` ad-hoc diagnostic with a tracked, reviewable source-feasibility artifact: it is probe-only, gated by `--confirm-fetch-authorized`, refuses `result/a_short`, keeps `backtest_evidence_capable=false`, and its pure classifier/summary consistency tests cover future-date, bad-date, bad-shape, quiet, transport-failure, forged-reachable, and forged-feasible cases. However the current real-fetch path overclaims source-quality auditing. The active contract / README / schema / runner state that the EM probe "re-validates every returned item itself", "does NOT trust `fetch_em_news`' own window filter", partitions `n_recent` / `n_future` / `n_stale` / `n_bad_date` / `n_bad_shape`, and that `future_dated_rejection` proves zero future leak. In the actual CLI path, `runners/a_short_em_news_probe.py::main()` calls the existing `fetch_em_news`; that function normalizes the EM payload and filters it to `recent = [n for n in norm if _em_news_in_window(...)]` before returning `items` to the probe. Future-dated, stale, and malformed/unparseable items can therefore be dropped before `classify_em_code()` ever sees them. The tests inject raw future / bad-shape items directly into `classify_em_code()` / `assess_em_feasibility()`, so they prove the classifier rejects visible defects, but they do not prove the real fetcher-to-probe path preserves those defects for counting. Materiality: a real EM response containing future-dated or malformed rows can be silently filtered by the shared weekly fetcher, while the probe summary still records `n_future_leak_codes=0`, `n_bad_date_codes=0`, `future_dated_rejection=true`, and possibly `feasible=true`; this reintroduces a source-evidence overclaim exactly in the artifact meant to close the EM audit gap. Required repair: either add a probe-specific EM fetch path / mode that returns the normalized unfiltered EM item stream plus enough shape/date metadata for `classify_em_code()` to count future / stale / bad-date / bad-shape rows, or downgrade the contract/schema/README/runner language and fields so the tracked probe claims only reachability and recent-news coverage over the already-filtered `fetch_em_news` output, not future-leak / bad-shape auditing. Add regression coverage that exercises the real fetcher-to-probe integration (mock EM HTTP/session or injected fetcher at the same abstraction boundary) with future-dated and malformed EM rows and proves they either fail the probe gates or are no longer claimed as audited. Boundary: source-feasibility probe, schema, docs, and tests only; do not change DeepSeek judgment semantics, M6.7 advisory behavior, official_structured semantics, production EGS scoring/ranking, V14.2, historical backtests, broker/order behavior, or run real web fetches in tests. Closure requires the repaired targeted EM probe tests, contract/README/schema drift guard if claims are changed, `py_compile`, schema parse, `git diff --check`, and no ad-hoc `_diag_web_sources.py` / validation byproduct staged. **Addressed (Claude `修复` 2026-06-14, option A = preserve auditing, not downgrade)**: added a probe-specific unfiltered fetcher `fetch_em_news_unfiltered` in `runners/a_short_em_news_probe.py` — same em endpoint/request as production `fetch_em_news` (reuses the endpoint constants + `_strip_jsonp`), but returns the normalized-but-UNFILTERED item stream (NO `_em_news_in_window` PIT/recency filter, no sort/cap; em `date`→`published_at` kept even when empty; non-dict rows kept) so `classify_em_code` actually sees future / stale / bad-date / bad-shape rows; `main()` now defaults to it (`news_fetcher or fetch_em_news_unfiltered`, fetcher signature `(codes, names)`). Production weekly still uses the FILTERED `fetch_em_news` (untouched — boundary held). Added integration regression class `FetchEmNewsUnfiltered` (5 tests) exercising the REAL fetcher→probe path: a future-dated + a bad-shape raw EM row are PRESERVED (5 items, not pre-filtered) and counted (`n_future`/`n_bad_shape`) → code `unknown`; a 15-code pool with one future-leak code → `n_future_leak_codes=1`, `future_dated_rejection=false`, `feasible=false`; clean-recent → reachable; non-dict → bad_shape; no-name / non-200 fail-closed. Updated the now-accurate claims on every active surface: runner docstring + `classify` section comment, schema `description`, contract §web_llm EM-owner bullet (probe 走 unfiltered；weekly 生产用过滤版 `fetch_em_news`，probe 绝不复用), README owner row (UNFILTERED probe fetch + filtered-prod-not-reused). Verify: `tests.test_a_short_em_news_probe` 41 OK; with guards 139 OK (em probe + contract-docs drift guard + doc governance + route-doc ledger + existing semantic probe — contract/README/schema edits trip no EM-drift / run-path / governance guard); schema Draft7 OK; `py_compile` OK; 5 changed files no-BOM; `git diff --check` clean (only LF/CRLF warnings); `git status` = 4 docs M (README/contract/SESSION_LOG/register) + 3 new (runner/schema/test), no `_diag_web_sources.py` / `_em_slice.patch` / byproduct staged. CURRENT MECHANISM (final — narrowest strategy):
- `RISK_KEYWORD_MAP` carries `severity` (high 立案/处罚/ST · medium 监管函件/关注/资金占用/担保 · low 诉讼/仲裁); official_structured events carry `severity` (schema enum high/medium/low).

- Everything else → risk for the 2b-ii skill to downgrade: a bare routine report WITHOUT an explicit negation (incl. the exact 浦发 专项说明 / 关联资金往来情况汇总表) surfaces as `risk[medium]`; explicit/suspected occupation (存在/发生/被…占用) and 整改/违规担保/问询/立案/处罚 → risk. **Property: residual errors are false-positives only (skill downgrades), never 漏报** (a missed negation word merely shows one no-occupation report as risk — harmless). Tested both ways (`test_only_routine_form_WITH_negation_is_suppressed` clears 不存在/未发生/无新增/不存在被…占用; `test_bare_routine_without_negation_now_surfaces_as_risk` + `test_explicit_or_suspected_occupation_surfaces_as_risk`).

Panel WIRING into the weekly pipeline deferred (render function only here).

A-short semantic-risk provider probe reports provider-quality-invalid cninfo rows as `clear_light` (status `resolved` Claude `修复` + Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12; severity `P2`; scope `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `tests/test_a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_semantic_risk_probe_summary.schema.json` if status enum is extended, `docs/README.md`; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk Slice-1 / per-code status semantics / unknown-not-clear`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-SEMANTIC-PROBE-CNINFO-BAD-ROW-CLEAR-STATUS`): the P1 feasibility bypass is repaired, but `classify_cninfo_code` still sets `status="clear_light"` whenever `ok=True` and there is no PIT-valid announcement, even if the provider returned future-dated rows, unparseable disclosure dates, or non-dict malformed rows. Codex synthetic no-network probes after the latest repair show `future`, `bad_date`, and `bad_shape` samples now correctly produce `feasible=false` and reject forged `feasible=true`, but the affected per-code object still reports `status='clear_light'` with `dates_pit_ok=false` and one of `n_future_dated` / `n_unparseable_dates` / `n_bad_shape` > 0. That is not "successfully checked and clear"; it is an unknown / provider-quality-invalid state and contradicts the design/route wording that failure/unknown must not be disguised as clear. The same semantic hole can exist for PIT rows whose required fields or `secCode` mapping fail: feasibility blocks, but the per-code status can still read `clear_light`. Required repair: define and enforce status semantics so `clear_light` is allowed only for a genuinely successful clear result (empty successful window, or PIT-clean non-risk rows with required fields and mapping valid). Any code with future rows, unparseable dates, malformed rows, missing required fields, or code-mapping mismatch must be `unknown` or a formally added invalid-status enum. If using `unknown`, update `_check_provider_counts` so `ok=True` provider-quality failures may be `unknown`, while transport failures still must be `unknown`. Add adversarial tests for future-only, unparseable-only, non-dict-only, missing-field, and mapping-mismatch rows not being `clear_light`, plus a consistency test that a summary containing such an invalid row labelled `clear_light` raises. No real provider fetch or production behavior is authorized by this finding. **Working-tree repaired (Claude `修复` 2026-06-12, reused `unknown`)**: `classify_cninfo_code` now computes `quality_ok = (no future/unparseable/non-dict defects AND n_pit>0 AND required_fields_ok AND code_mapping_ok)` and assigns `status` as: not ok → `unknown`; ok + empty window → `clear_light`; ok + not quality_ok → `unknown`; ok + quality_ok + risk-keyword → `risk_candidate`; else `clear_light`. So future/unparseable/non-dict/missing-field/mapping-mismatch codes now read `unknown`, never `clear`. `_check_provider_counts` relaxed: the strict `ok ⇔ not-unknown` invariant became `not ok ⇒ unknown` (transport failure) for both providers + a cninfo per-code status-quality invariant (clear_light/risk_candidate require ok + clean + valid fields/mapping; risk_candidate requires PIT rows) while sina keeps `ok ⇒ not unknown`. Adversarial tests added (future / unparseable / non-dict / missing-field / mapping-mismatch → status `unknown`; + consistency test that a defective row labelled `clear_light` raises). Status enum unchanged (reused `unknown`); 44 tests pass; schema meta + py_compile OK. Resolved: Codex re-`审查` PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12.

A-short semantic-risk provider probe ignores unparseable / malformed cninfo returned rows in feasibility gate (status `resolved` Claude `修复` + Codex PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12; severity `P1`; scope `runners/a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `tests/test_a_short_semantic_risk_probe.py`, `schemas/a_short_semantic_risk_probe_summary.schema.json` if fields are added; PIT label `A-short semantic-risk Slice-1 / cninfo provider-shape and disclosure-date gate`; Required ID `R-ASHORT-SEMANTIC-PROBE-CNINFO-BAD-DATE-SHAPE-BYPASS`): the future-date PIT leak was repaired, but returned rows with bad shape can still bypass feasibility. `classify_cninfo_code` filters `announcements` to dict rows before counting `n_returned`, so non-dict provider rows vanish completely. Rows with unparseable `announcementTime` set per-code `dates_pit_ok=False`, but because they yield `n_announcements=0`, they are excluded from the aggregate `announced` set and do not affect `n_dates_pit_ok`; a sample with 4 clean PIT-announced codes plus one unparseable-date returned row still produced `feasible=True`, no blocking reasons, and that bad-date code status `clear_light`. A sample with 4 clean PIT-announced codes plus one non-dict announcement row also produced `feasible=True` after silently treating the malformed row as no return. This violates the Slice-1 goal of proving cninfo field/date shape before Slice 2. Required repair: count raw returned items before filtering, expose and gate invalid returned rows (`n_unparseable_date_codes` / `n_bad_shape_codes` or equivalent), and ensure non-dict rows or unparseable disclosure dates cannot be reported as clean and cannot coexist with `feasible=True`. No real provider fetch or production behavior is authorized by this finding. **Working-tree repaired (Claude `修复` 2026-06-12)**: `classify_cninfo_code` now counts `n_returned` on the RAW provider list BEFORE any `isinstance` filter, and partitions every returned row exactly into `n_announcements`(PIT dict+canonical+≤as_of) + `n_future_dated` + `n_unparseable_dates`(dict, bad/missing date) + `n_bad_shape`(non-dict), with a consistency assert that the four sum to `n_returned`; non-dict rows are no longer silently dropped. Three provider quality gates (`n_future_dated_codes==0`, `n_unparseable_date_codes==0`, `n_bad_shape_codes==0`) are now feasibility AND consistency conditions, so a malformed/unparseable/future row can neither be reported clean (`dates_pit_ok` == "all returned rows clean") nor coexist with `feasible=true`. Adversarial tests added: unparseable-date row counted-not-dropped, non-dict row counted-not-dropped, partition-sums-to-n_returned, and the exact Codex repros (4 clean + 1 unparseable-date code → feasible=false + reason; 4 clean + 1 non-dict-row code → feasible=false + reason). 43 tests pass; schema + consistency updated. Resolved: Codex re-`审查` PASS + committed local master 2026-06-12.
